title: Gender of Nouns
text:
There are three Genders,—Masculine, Feminine, and Neuter. Gender in Latin is either natural or grammatical.
⟦b:Natural Gender.⟧
The gender of nouns is natural when it is based upon sex. Natural gender is confined entirely to names of persons; and these are—
1. Masculine, if they denote males; as,—
⟦b:nauta⟧, ⟦i:sailor⟧; ⟦b:agricola⟧, ⟦i:farmer⟧.
2. Feminine, if they denote females; as,—
⟦b:māter⟧, ⟦i:mother⟧; ⟦b:rēgīna⟧, ⟦i:queen⟧.
⟦b:Grammatical Gender.⟧
Grammatical gender is determined not by sex, but by the general signification of the word, or the ending of its Nominative Singular. By grammatical gender, nouns denoting things or qualities are often Masculine or Feminine, simply by virtue of their signification or the ending of the Nominative Singular. The following are the general principles for determining grammatical gender:—
⟦i:A. Gender determined by Signification.⟧
1. Names of ⟦i:Rivers⟧, ⟦i:Winds⟧, and ⟦i:Months⟧ are Masculine; as,—
⟦b:Sēquana⟧, ⟦i:Seine⟧; ⟦b:Eurus⟧, ⟦i:east wind⟧; ⟦b:Aprīlis⟧, ⟦i:April⟧.
2. Names of ⟦i:Trees⟧, and such names of ⟦i:Towns⟧ and ⟦i:Islands⟧ as end in ⟦b:-us⟧, are Feminine; as,—
⟦b:quercus⟧, ⟦i:oak⟧; ⟦b:Corinthus⟧, ⟦i:Corinth⟧; ⟦b:Rhodus⟧, ⟦i:Rhodes⟧.
Other names of towns and islands follow the gender of their endings (see ⟦i:B⟧, below); as,—
⟦b:Delphī⟧, n.; ⟦b:Leuctra⟧, n.; ⟦b:Tībur⟧, n.; ⟦b:Carthāgō⟧, f.
3. Indeclinable nouns, also infinitives and phrases, are Neuter; as,—
⟦b:nihil⟧, ⟦i:nothing⟧; ⟦b:nefās⟧, ⟦i:wrong⟧; ⟦b:amāre⟧, ⟦i:to love⟧.
NOTE.—Exceptions to the above principles sometimes occur; as, ⟦b:Allia⟧ (the river), f.
⟦i:B. Gender determined by Ending of Nominative Singular.⟧
The gender of other nouns is determined by the ending of the Nominative Singular.
NOTE 1.—⟦i:Common Gender.⟧ Certain nouns are sometimes Masculine, sometimes Feminine. Thus, ⟦b:sacerdōs⟧ may mean either ⟦i:priest⟧ or ⟦i:priestess⟧, and is Masculine or Feminine accordingly. So also ⟦b:cīvis⟧, ⟦i:citizen⟧; ⟦b:parēns⟧, ⟦i:parent⟧; etc. The gender of such nouns is said to be ⟦i:common⟧.
NOTE 2.—Names of animals usually have grammatical gender, according to the ending of the Nominative Singular, but the one form may designate either the male or female; as, ⟦b:ānser⟧, m., ⟦i:goose⟧ or ⟦i:gander⟧. So ⟦b:vulpēs⟧, f., ⟦i:fox⟧; ⟦b:aquīla⟧, f., ⟦i:eagle⟧.

title: Cases
The Five Declensions
text:
There are five Declensions in Latin, distinguished from each other by the final letter of the Stem, and also by the Termination of the Genitive Singular, as follows:—
DECLENSION.  FINAL LETTER OF STEM.  GEN. TERMINATION.
⟦b:First⟧  ⟦b:ā⟧  ⟦b:-ae⟧
⟦b:Second⟧  ⟦b:ŏ⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦b:Third⟧  ⟦b:ĭ⟧ / ⟦b:Some consonant⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧
⟦b:Fourth⟧  ⟦b:ŭ⟧  ⟦b:-ūs⟧
⟦b:Fifth⟧  ⟦b:ē⟧  ⟦b:-ēī⟧ / ⟦b:-ĕī⟧
⟦/⟧
Cases alike in Form.
1. The Vocative is regularly like the Nominative, except in the singular of nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧ of the Second Declension.
2. The Dative and Ablative Plural are always alike.
3. In Neuters the Accusative and Nominative are always alike, and in the Plural end in ⟦b:-ă⟧.
4. In the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Declensions, the Accusative Plural is regularly like the Nominative.
ā-Stems.

title: First Declension
text:
Pure Latin nouns of the First Declension regularly end, in the Nominative Singular, in ⟦b:-ă⟧, weakened from ⟦b:-ā⟧, and are of the Feminine Gender. They are declined as follows:—
⟦=⟧⟦b:Porta⟧, ⟦i:gate⟧; stem, ⟦b:portā-⟧.  SINGULAR.
CASES.  ⟦.⟧  MEANINGS.  TERMINATIONS.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  port⟦b:a⟧  ⟦i:a gate⟧ (as subject)  ⟦b:-ă⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  port⟦b:ae⟧  ⟦i:of a gate⟧  ⟦b:-ae⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  port⟦b:ae⟧  ⟦i:to⟧ or ⟦i:for a gate⟧  ⟦b:-ae⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  port⟦b:am⟧  ⟦i:a gate⟧ (as object)  ⟦b:-am⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  port⟦b:a⟧  ⟦i:O gate!⟧  ⟦b:-ă⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  port⟦b:ā⟧  ⟦i:with, by, from, in a gate⟧  ⟦b:-ā⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  port⟦b:ae⟧  ⟦i:gates⟧ (as subject)  ⟦b:-ae⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  port⟦b:ārum⟧  ⟦i:of gates⟧  ⟦b:-ārum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  port⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦i:to⟧ or ⟦i:for gates⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  port⟦b:ās⟧  ⟦i:gates⟧ (as object)  ⟦b:-ās⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  port⟦b:ae⟧  ⟦i:O gates!⟧  ⟦b:-ae⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  port⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦i:with, by, from, in gates⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧
⟦/⟧
1. The Latin has no article, and ⟦b:porta⟧ may mean either ⟦i:a gate⟧ or ⟦i:the gate⟧; and in the Plural, ⟦i:gates⟧ or ⟦i:the gates⟧.
Peculiarities of Nouns of the First Declension.
1. EXCEPTIONS IN GENDER. Nouns denoting males are Masculine; as, ⟦b:nauta⟧, ⟦i:sailor⟧; ⟦b:agricola⟧, ⟦i:farmer⟧; also, ⟦b:Hadria⟧, ⟦i:Adriatic Sea⟧.
2. Rare Case-Endings,—
⟦i:a⟧) An old form of the Genitive Singular in ⟦b:-ās⟧ is preserved in the combination ⟦b:pater familiās⟧, ⟦i:father of a family⟧; also in ⟦b:māter familiās⟧, ⟦b:fīlius familiās⟧, ⟦b:fīlia familiās⟧. But the regular form of the Genitive in ⟦b:-ae⟧ is also admissible in these expressions; as, ⟦b:pater familiae⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) In poetry a Genitive in ⟦b:-āī⟧ also occurs; as, ⟦b:aulāī⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) The Locative Singular ends in ⟦b:-ae⟧; as, ⟦b:Rōmae⟧, ⟦i:at Rome⟧.
⟦i:d⟧) A Genitive Plural in ⟦b:-um⟧ instead of ⟦b:-ārum⟧ sometimes occurs; as, ⟦b:Dardanidum⟧ instead of ⟦b:Dardanidārum⟧. This termination ⟦b:-um⟧ is not a contraction of ⟦b:-ārum⟧, but represents an entirely different case-ending.
⟦i:e⟧) Instead of the regular ending ⟦b:-īs⟧, we usually find ⟦b:-ābus⟧ in the Dative and Ablative Plural of ⟦b:dea⟧, ⟦i:goddess⟧, and ⟦b:fīlia⟧, ⟦i:daughter⟧, especially when it is important to distinguish these nouns from the corresponding forms of ⟦b:deus⟧, ⟦i:god⟧, and ⟦b:fīlius⟧, ⟦i:son⟧. A few other words sometimes have the same peculiarity; as, ⟦b:lībertābus⟧ (from ⟦b:līberta⟧, ⟦i:freedwoman⟧), ⟦b:equābus⟧ (⟦i:mares⟧), to avoid confusion with ⟦b:lībertīs⟧ (from ⟦b:lībertus⟧, ⟦i:freedman⟧) and ⟦b:equīs⟧ (from ⟦b:equus⟧, ⟦i:horse⟧).
Greek Nouns.
These end in ⟦b:-ē⟧ (Feminine); ⟦b:-ās⟧ and ⟦b:-ēs⟧ (Masculine). In the Plural they are declined like regular Latin nouns of the First Declension. In the Singular they are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Archiās⟧, ⟦i:Archias⟧.  ⟦b:Epitomē⟧, ⟦i:epitome⟧.  ⟦b:Comētēs⟧, ⟦i:comet⟧.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  Archi⟦b:ās⟧  epitom⟦b:ē⟧  comēt⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  Archi⟦b:ae⟧  epitom⟦b:ēs⟧  comēt⟦b:ae⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  Archi⟦b:ae⟧  epitom⟦b:ae⟧  comēt⟦b:ae⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  Archi⟦b:am⟧ (or ⟦b:-ān⟧)  epitom⟦b:ēn⟧  comēt⟦b:ēn⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  Archi⟦b:ā⟧  epitom⟦b:ē⟧  comēt⟦b:ē⟧ (or ⟦b:-ă⟧)
⟦i:Abl.⟧  Archi⟦b:ā⟧  epitom⟦b:ē⟧  comēt⟦b:ē⟧ (or ⟦b:-ā⟧)
⟦/⟧
1. But most Greek nouns in ⟦b:-ē⟧ become regular Latin nouns in ⟦b:-a⟧, and are declined like ⟦b:porta⟧; as, ⟦b:grammatica⟧, ⟦i:grammar⟧; ⟦b:mūsica⟧, ⟦i:music⟧; ⟦b:rhētorica⟧, ⟦i:rhetoric⟧.
2. Some other peculiarities occur, especially in poetry.
ŏ-Stems.

title: Second Declension
text:
Pure Latin nouns of the Second Declension end in ⟦b:-us⟧, ⟦b:-er⟧, ⟦b:-ir⟧, Masculine; ⟦b:-um⟧, Neuter. Originally ⟦b:-us⟧ in the Nominative of the Masculine was ⟦b:-os⟧; and ⟦b:-um⟧ of the Neuters ⟦b:-om⟧. So also in the Accusative.
Nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧ and ⟦b:-um⟧ are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Hortus⟧, ⟦i:garden⟧; stem, ⟦b:hortŏ-⟧.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Bellum⟧, ⟦i:war⟧; stem, ⟦b:bellŏ-⟧.
⟦=⟧SINGULAR.
⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  TERMINATION.  ⟦.⟧  TERMINATION.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  hort⟦b:us⟧  ⟦b:-us⟧  bell⟦b:um⟧  ⟦b:-um⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  hort⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧  bell⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  hort⟦b:ō⟧  ⟦b:-ō⟧  bell⟦b:ō⟧  ⟦b:-ō⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  hort⟦b:um⟧  ⟦b:-um⟧  bell⟦b:um⟧  ⟦b:-um⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  hort⟦b:e⟧  ⟦b:-e⟧  bell⟦b:um⟧  ⟦b:-um⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  hort⟦b:ō⟧  ⟦b:-ō⟧  bell⟦b:ō⟧  ⟦b:-ō⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  hort⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧  bell⟦b:a⟧  ⟦b:-a⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  hort⟦b:ōrum⟧  ⟦b:-ōrum⟧  bell⟦b:ōrum⟧  ⟦b:-ōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  hort⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧  bell⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  hort⟦b:ōs⟧  ⟦b:-ōs⟧  bell⟦b:a⟧  ⟦b:-a⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  hort⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧  bell⟦b:a⟧  ⟦b:-a⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  hort⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧  bell⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧
⟦/⟧
Nouns in ⟦b:-er⟧ and ⟦b:-ir⟧ are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Puer⟧, ⟦i:boy⟧; stem, ⟦b:puerŏ-⟧  ⟦b:Ager⟧, ⟦i:field⟧; stem, ⟦b:agrŏ-⟧  ⟦b:Vir⟧, ⟦i:man⟧; stem, ⟦b:virŏ-⟧
SINGULAR.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  TERMINATION.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  puer  ager  vir  Wanting
⟦i:Gen.⟧  puer⟦b:ī⟧  agr⟦b:ī⟧  vir⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  puer⟦b:ō⟧  agr⟦b:ō⟧  vir⟦b:ō⟧  ⟦b:-ō⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  puer⟦b:um⟧  agr⟦b:um⟧  vir⟦b:um⟧  ⟦b:-um⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  puer  ager  vir  Wanting
⟦i:Abl.⟧  puer⟦b:ō⟧  agr⟦b:ō⟧  vir⟦b:ō⟧  ⟦b:-ō⟧
PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  puer⟦b:ī⟧  agr⟦b:ī⟧  vir⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  puer⟦b:ōrum⟧  agr⟦b:ōrum⟧  vir⟦b:ōrum⟧  ⟦b:-ōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  puer⟦b:īs⟧  agr⟦b:īs⟧  vir⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  puer⟦b:ōs⟧  agr⟦b:ōs⟧  vir⟦b:ōs⟧  ⟦b:-ōs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  puer⟦b:ī⟧  agr⟦b:ī⟧  vir⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  puer⟦b:īs⟧  agr⟦b:īs⟧  vir⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧
⟦/⟧
1. Note that in words of the type of ⟦b:puer⟧ and ⟦b:vir⟧ the final vowel of the stem has disappeared in the Nominative and Vocative Singular.
In the Nominative and Vocative Singular of ⟦b:ager⟧, the stem is further modified by the development of ⟦b:e⟧ before ⟦b:r⟧.
2. The following nouns in ⟦b:-er⟧ are declined like ⟦b:puer⟧: ⟦b:adulter⟧, ⟦i:adulterer⟧; ⟦b:gener⟧, ⟦i:son-in-law⟧; ⟦b:Līber⟧, ⟦i:Bacchus⟧; ⟦b:socer⟧, ⟦i:father-in-law⟧; ⟦b:vesper⟧, ⟦i:evening⟧; and compounds in ⟦b:-fer⟧ and ⟦b:-ger⟧, as ⟦b:signifer⟧, ⟦b:armiger⟧.
Nouns in ⟦i:-vus⟧, ⟦i:-vum⟧, ⟦i:-quus⟧.
Nouns ending in the Nominative Singular in ⟦b:-vus⟧, ⟦b:-vum⟧, ⟦b:-quus⟧, exhibited two types of inflection in the classical Latin,—an earlier and a later,—as follows:—
⟦=⟧⟦i:Earlier Inflection (including Caesar and Cicero).⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Servos⟧, m., ⟦i:slave⟧.  ⟦b:Aevom⟧, n., ⟦i:age⟧.  ⟦b:Equos⟧, m., ⟦i:horse⟧.
⟦=⟧SINGULAR.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  servos  aevom  equos
⟦i:Gen.⟧  servī  aevī  equī
⟦i:Dat.⟧  servō  aevō  equō
⟦i:Acc.⟧  servom  aevom  equom
⟦i:Voc.⟧  serve  aevom  eque
⟦i:Abl.⟧  servō  aevō  equō
⟦=⟧⟦i:Later inflection (after Cicero).⟧  SINGULAR.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  servus  aevum  equus
⟦i:Gen.⟧  servī  aevī  equī
⟦i:Dat.⟧  servō  aevō  equō
⟦i:Act.⟧  servum  aevum  equum
⟦i:Voc.⟧  serve  aevum  eque
⟦i:Abl.⟧  servō  aevō  equō
⟦/⟧
1. The Plural of these nouns is regular, and always uniform.
Peculiarities of Inflection in the Second Declension.
1. Proper names in ⟦b:-ius⟧ regularly form the Genitive Singular in ⟦b:-ī⟧ (instead of ⟦b:-iī⟧), and the Vocative Singular in ⟦b:-ī⟧ (for ⟦b:-ie⟧); as ⟦b:Vergílī⟧, ⟦i:of Virgil⟧, or ⟦i:O Virgil⟧ (instead of ⟦b:Vergiliī⟧, ⟦b:Vergilie⟧). In such words the accent stands upon the penult, even though that be short. Nouns in ⟦b:-ajus⟧, ⟦b:-ejus⟧ form the Gen. in ⟦b:-aī⟧, ⟦b:-eī⟧, as ⟦b:Pompejus⟧, ⟦b:Pompeī⟧.
2. Nouns in ⟦b:-ius⟧ and ⟦b:-ium⟧, until after the beginning of the reign of Augustus (31 B.C.), regularly formed the Genitive Singular in ⟦b:-i⟧ (instead of ⟦b:-iī⟧); as,—
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:ingenium⟧  ⟦b:fīlius⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:ingénī⟧  ⟦b:fīlī⟧
⟦/⟧
These Genitives accent the penult, even when it is short.
3. ⟦b:Fīlius⟧ forms the Vocative Singular in ⟦b:-ī⟧ (for ⟦b:-ie⟧); ⟦i:viz⟧. ⟦b:fīlī⟧, ⟦i:O son!⟧
4. ⟦b:Deus⟧, ⟦i:god⟧, lacks the Vocative Singular. The Plural is inflected as follows:—
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:dī⟧  ⟦b:(deī)⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:deōrum⟧  ⟦b:(deum)⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:dīs⟧  ⟦b:(deīs)⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:deōs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  ⟦b:dī⟧  ⟦b:(deī)⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:dīs⟧  ⟦b:(deīs)⟧
⟦/⟧
5. The Locative Singular ends in ⟦b:-ī⟧; as, ⟦b:Corinthī⟧, ⟦i:at Corinth⟧.
6. The Genitive Plural has ⟦b:-um⟧, instead of ⟦b:-ōrum⟧,—
⟦i:a⟧) in words denoting money and measure; as, ⟦b:talentum⟧, ⟦i:of talents⟧; ⟦b:modium⟧, ⟦i:of pecks⟧; ⟦b:sēstertium⟧, ⟦i:of sesterces⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) in ⟦b:duumvir⟧, ⟦b:triumvir⟧, ⟦b:decemvir⟧; as, ⟦b:duumvirum⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) sometimes in other words; as, ⟦b:līberum⟧, ⟦i:of the children⟧; ⟦b:socium⟧, ⟦i:of the allies⟧.
Exceptions to Gender in the Second Declension.
1. The following nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧ are Feminine by exception:—
⟦i:a⟧) Names of ⟦b:towns⟧, ⟦b:islands⟧, ⟦b:trees⟧—according to the general rule laid down in § 15, 2; also some names of countries; as ⟦b:Aegyptus⟧, ⟦i:Egypt⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) Five special words,—
⟦b:alvus⟧, ⟦i:belly⟧;
⟦b:carbasus⟧, ⟦i:flax⟧;
⟦b:colus⟧, ⟦i:distaff⟧;
⟦b:humus⟧, ⟦i:ground⟧;
⟦b:vannus⟧, ⟦i:winnowing-fan⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) A few Greek Feminines; as,—
⟦b:atomus⟧, ⟦i:atom⟧;
⟦b:diphthongus⟧, ⟦i:diphthong⟧.
2. The following nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧ are Neuter:—
⟦b:pelagus⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧;
⟦b:vīrus⟧, ⟦i:poison⟧;
⟦b:vulgus⟧, ⟦i:crowd⟧.
Greek Nouns of the Second Declension.
These end in ⟦b:-os⟧, ⟦b:-ōs⟧, Masculine or Feminine; and ⟦b:-on⟧, Neuter. They are mainly proper names, and are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Barbitos⟧, m. and f., ⟦i:lyre.⟧  ⟦b:Androgeōs⟧, m., ⟦i:Androgeos.⟧  ⟦b:Īlion⟧, n., ⟦i:Troy.⟧
⟦i:Nom.⟧  barbit⟦b:os⟧  Androge⟦b:ōs⟧  Īli⟦b:on⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  barbit⟦b:ī⟧  Androge⟦b:ō⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧  Īli⟦b:ī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  barbit⟦b:ō⟧  Androge⟦b:ō⟧  Īli⟦b:ō⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  barbit⟦b:on⟧  Androge⟦b:ō⟧, ⟦b:-ōn⟧  Īli⟦b:on⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  barbit⟦b:e⟧  Androge⟦b:ōs⟧  Īli⟦b:on⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  barbit⟦b:ō⟧  Androge⟦b:ō⟧  Īli⟦b:ō⟧
⟦/⟧
1. Nouns in ⟦b:-os⟧ sometimes form the Accusative Singular in ⟦b:-um⟧ instead of ⟦b:-on⟧; as, ⟦b:Dēlum⟧, ⟦i:Delos⟧.
2. The Plural of Greek nouns, when it occurs, is usually regular.
3. For other rare forms of Greek nouns the lexicon may be consulted.

title: Third Declension
text:
Nouns of the Third Declension end in ⟦b:-a⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦b:-ō⟧, ⟦b:-y⟧, ⟦b:-c⟧, ⟦b:-l⟧, ⟦b:-n⟧, ⟦b:-r⟧, ⟦b:-s⟧, ⟦b:-t⟧, ⟦b:-x.⟧ The Third Declension includes several distinct classes of Stems,—
I.  Pure Consonant-Stems.
II.  ĭ-Stems.
III.  Consonant-Stems which have partially adapted themselves to the inflection of ĭ-Stems.
IV.  A very few stems ending in a long vowel or a diphthong.
V.  Irregular Nouns.
⟦/⟧
I. Consonant-Stems.
1. In these the stem appears in its unaltered form in all the oblique cases, so that the actual case-endings may be clearly recognized.
2. Consonant-Stems fall into several natural subdivisions, according as the stem ends in a ⟦b:Mute⟧, ⟦b:Liquid⟧, ⟦b:Nasal⟧, or ⟦b:Spirant⟧.
⟦i:A. Mute-Stems.⟧
Mute-Stems may end,—
1. In a Labial (⟦b:p⟧); as, ⟦b:prīncep-s⟧.
2. In a Guttural (⟦b:g⟧ or ⟦b:c⟧); as, ⟦b:rēmex⟧ (⟦b:rēmeg-s⟧); ⟦b:dux⟧ (⟦b:duc-s⟧).
3. In a Dental (⟦b:d⟧ or ⟦b:t⟧); as, ⟦b:lapis⟧ (⟦b:lapid-s⟧); ⟦b:mīles⟧ (⟦b:mīlet-s⟧).
1. STEMS IN A LABIAL MUTE (⟦b:p⟧).
⟦b:Prīnceps⟧, m., ⟦i:chief⟧.
⟦.⟧  SINGULAR.  TERMINATION.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  prīncep⟦b:s⟧  ⟦b:-s⟧

⟦i:Dat.⟧  prīncip⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  prīncip⟦b:em⟧  ⟦b:-em⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  prīncep⟦b:s⟧  ⟦b:-s⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  prīncip⟦b:e⟧  ⟦b:-e⟧
⟦.⟧  PLURAL.

⟦/⟧
2. STEMS IN A GUTTURAL MUTE (⟦b:g⟧, ⟦b:c⟧).
In these the termination ⟦b:-s⟧ of the Nominative Singular unites with the guttural, thus producing ⟦b:-x⟧.
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Rēmex⟧, m., ⟦i:rower⟧.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Dux⟧, c., ⟦i:leader⟧.
⟦.⟧  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  rēme⟦b:x⟧  rēmig⟦b:ēs⟧  du⟦b:x⟧  duc⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  rēmig⟦b:is⟧  rēmig⟦b:um⟧  duc⟦b:is⟧  duc⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  rēmig⟦b:ī⟧  rēmig⟦b:ibus⟧  duc⟦b:ī⟧  duc⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  rēmig⟦b:em⟧  rēmig⟦b:ēs⟧  duc⟦b:em⟧  duc⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  rēme⟦b:x⟧  rēmig⟦b:ēs⟧  du⟦b:x⟧  duc⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  rēmig⟦b:e⟧  rēmig⟦b:ibus⟧  duc⟦b:e⟧  duc⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
3. STEMS IN A DENTAL MUTE (⟦b:d⟧, ⟦b:t⟧).
In these the final ⟦b:d⟧ or ⟦b:t⟧ of the stem disappears in the Nominative Singular before the ending ⟦b:-s⟧.
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Lapis⟧, m., ⟦i:stone⟧.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Mīles⟧, m., ⟦i:soldier⟧.
⟦.⟧  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  lapi⟦b:s⟧  lapid⟦b:ēs⟧  mīle⟦b:s⟧  mīlit⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  lapid⟦b:is⟧  lapid⟦b:um⟧  mīlit⟦b:is⟧  mīlit⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  lapid⟦b:ī⟧  lapid⟦b:ibus⟧  mīlit⟦b:ī⟧  mīlit⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  lapid⟦b:em⟧  lapid⟦b:ēs⟧  mīlit⟦b:em⟧  mīlit⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  lapi⟦b:s⟧  lapid⟦b:ēs⟧  mīle⟦b:s⟧  mīlit⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  lapid⟦b:e⟧  lapid⟦b:ibus⟧  mīlit⟦b:e⟧  mīlit⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦i:B. Liquid Stems.⟧
These end in ⟦b:-l⟧ or ⟦b:-r⟧.
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Vigil⟧, m., ⟦i:watchman⟧.  ⟦b:Victor⟧, m., ⟦i:conqueror⟧.  ⟦b:Aequor⟧, n., ⟦i:sea⟧.
⟦=⟧SINGULAR.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  vigil  victor  aequor
⟦i:Gen.⟧  vigil⟦b:is⟧  victōr⟦b:is⟧  aequor⟦b:is⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  vigil⟦b:ī⟧  victōr⟦b:ī⟧  aequor⟦b:ī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  vigil⟦b:em⟧  victōr⟦b:em⟧  aequor
⟦i:Voc.⟧  vigil  victor  aequor
⟦i:Abl.⟧  vigil⟦b:e⟧  victōr⟦b:e⟧  aequor⟦b:e⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  vigil⟦b:ēs⟧  victōr⟦b:ēs⟧  aequor⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  vigil⟦b:um⟧  victōr⟦b:um⟧  aequor⟦b:um⟧

⟦i:Voc.⟧  vigil⟦b:ēs⟧  victōr⟦b:ēs⟧  aequor⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  vigil⟦b:ibus⟧  victōr⟦b:ibus⟧  aequor⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
1. Masculine and Feminine stems ending in a liquid form the Nominative and Vocative Singular without termination.
2. The termination is also lacking in the Nominative, Accusative and Vocative Singular of all ⟦b:neuters⟧ of the Third Declension.
⟦i:C. Nasal Stems.⟧
These end in ⟦b:-n⟧, which often disappears in the Nom. Sing.
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Leō⟧, m., ⟦i:lion⟧.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Nōmen⟧, n., ⟦i:name⟧
⟦.⟧  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  leō  leōn⟦b:ēs⟧  nōmen  nōmin⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  leōn⟦b:is⟧  leōn⟦b:um⟧  nōmin⟦b:is⟧  nōmin⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  leōn⟦b:ī⟧  leōn⟦b:ibus⟧  nōmin⟦b:ī⟧  nōmin⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  leōn⟦b:em⟧  leōn⟦b:ēs⟧  nōmen  nōmin⟦b:a⟧

⟦/⟧
⟦i:D. s-Stems.⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Mōs⟧, m. ⟦i:custom⟧.  ⟦b:Genus⟧, n., ⟦i:race⟧.  ⟦b:Honor⟧, m., ⟦i:honor⟧.
⟦=⟧SINGULAR.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  mōs  genus  honor
⟦i:Gen.⟧  mōr⟦b:is⟧  gener⟦b:is⟧  honōr⟦b:is⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  mōr⟦b:ī⟧  gener⟦b:ī⟧  honōr⟦b:ī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  mōr⟦b:em⟧  genus  honōr⟦b:em⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  mōs  genus  honor
⟦i:Abl.⟧  mōr⟦b:e⟧  gener⟦b:e⟧  honōr⟦b:e⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  mōr⟦b:ēs⟧  gener⟦b:a⟧  honōr⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  mōr⟦b:um⟧  gener⟦b:um⟧  honōr⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  mōr⟦b:ibus⟧  gener⟦b:ibus⟧  honōr⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  mōr⟦b:ēs⟧  gener⟦b:a⟧  honōr⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  mōr⟦b:ēs⟧  gener⟦b:a⟧  honōr⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  mōr⟦b:ibus⟧  gener⟦b:ibus⟧  honōr⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
1. Note that the final ⟦b:s⟧ of the stem becomes ⟦b:r⟧ (between vowels) in the oblique cases. In many words (⟦b:honor⟧, ⟦b:color⟧, and the like) the ⟦b:r⟧ of the oblique cases has, by analogy, crept into the Nominative, displacing the earlier ⟦b:s⟧, though the forms ⟦b:honōs⟧, ⟦b:colōs⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧, also occur, particularly in early Latin and in poetry.
II. ĭ-Stems.
⟦i:A. Masculine and Feminine⟧ ⟦b:ĭ⟧⟦i:-Stems.⟧
These regularly end in ⟦b:-is⟧ in the Nominative Singular, and always have ⟦b:-ium⟧ in the Genitive Plural. Originally the Accusative Singular ended in ⟦b:-im⟧, the Ablative Singular in ⟦b:-ī⟧, and the Accusative Plural in ⟦b:-īs⟧; but these endings have been largely displaced by ⟦b:-em⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, and ⟦b:-ēs⟧, the endings of Consonant-Stems.
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Tussis⟧, f., ⟦i:cough⟧; stem, ⟦b:tussi-⟧.  ⟦b:Īgnis⟧, m., ⟦i:fire⟧; stem, ⟦b:īgni-⟧.  ⟦b:Hostis⟧, c., ⟦i:enemy⟧; stem, ⟦b:hosti-⟧.
SINGULAR.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  TERMINATION.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  tuss⟦b:is⟧  īgn⟦b:is⟧  host⟦b:is⟧  ⟦b:-is⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  tuss⟦b:is⟧  īgn⟦b:is⟧  host⟦b:is⟧  ⟦b:-is⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  tuss⟦b:ī⟧  īgn⟦b:ī⟧  host⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  tuss⟦b:im⟧  īgn⟦b:em⟧  host⟦b:em⟧  ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦b:-em⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  tuss⟦b:is⟧  īgn⟦b:is⟧  host⟦b:is⟧  ⟦b:-is⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  tuss⟦b:ī⟧  īgn⟦b:ī⟧ or ⟦b:e⟧  host⟦b:e⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  tuss⟦b:ēs⟧  īgn⟦b:ēs⟧  host⟦b:ēs⟧  ⟦b:-ēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  tuss⟦b:ium⟧  īgn⟦b:ium⟧  host⟦b:ium⟧  ⟦b:-ium⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  tuss⟦b:ibus⟧  īgn⟦b:ibus⟧  host⟦b:ibus⟧  ⟦b:-ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  tuss⟦b:īs⟧ or ⟦b:-ēs⟧  īgn⟦b:īs⟧ or ⟦b:-ēs⟧  host⟦b:īs⟧ or ⟦b:-ēs⟧  ⟦b:-īs⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  tuss⟦b:ēs⟧  īgn⟦b:ēs⟧  host⟦b:ēs⟧  ⟦b:-ēs⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  tuss⟦b:ibus⟧  īgn⟦b:ibus⟧  host⟦b:ibus⟧  ⟦b:-ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
1. To the same class belong—
⟦b:apis⟧, ⟦i:bee⟧.  ⟦b:crātis⟧, ⟦i:hurdle⟧.  †*⟦b:secūris⟧, ⟦i:axe⟧.
⟦b:auris⟧, ⟦i:ear⟧.  *⟦b:febris⟧, ⟦i:fever⟧.  ⟦b:sēmentis⟧, ⟦i:sowing⟧.
⟦b:avis⟧, ⟦i:bird⟧.  ⟦b:orbis⟧, ⟦i:circle⟧.  †*⟦b:sitis⟧, ⟦i:thirst⟧.
⟦b:axis⟧, ⟦i:axle⟧.  ⟦b:ovis⟧, ⟦i:sheep⟧.  ⟦b:torris⟧, ⟦i:brand⟧.
*⟦b:būris⟧, ⟦i:plough-beam⟧.  ⟦b:pelvis⟧, ⟦i:basin⟧.  †*⟦b:turris⟧, ⟦i:tower⟧.
⟦b:clāvis⟧, ⟦i:key⟧.  ⟦b:puppis⟧, ⟦i:stern⟧.  ⟦b:trudis⟧, ⟦i:pole⟧.
⟦b:collis⟧, ⟦i:hill⟧.  ⟦b:restis⟧, ⟦i:rope⟧.  ⟦b:vectis⟧, ⟦i:lever⟧.
⟦.⟧  and many others.
⟦/⟧
Words marked with a star regularly have Acc. ⟦b:-im⟧; those marked with a † regularly have Abl. ⟦b:-ī⟧. Of the others, many at times show ⟦b:-im⟧ and ⟦b:-ī⟧. Town and river names in ⟦b:-is⟧ regularly have ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧.
2. Not all nouns in ⟦b:-is⟧ are ⟦b:ĭ⟧-Stems. Some are genuine consonant-stems, and have the regular consonant terminations throughout, notably, ⟦b:canis⟧, ⟦i:dog⟧; ⟦b:juvenis⟧, ⟦i:youth⟧.
3. Some genuine ⟦b:ĭ⟧-Stems have become disguised in the Nominative Singular; as, ⟦b:pars⟧, ⟦i:part⟧, for ⟦b:par(ti)s⟧; ⟦b:anas⟧, ⟦i:duck⟧, for ⟦b:ana(ti)s⟧; so also ⟦b:mors⟧, ⟦i:death⟧; ⟦b:dōs⟧, ⟦i:dowry⟧; ⟦b:nox⟧, ⟦i:night⟧; ⟦b:sors⟧, ⟦i:lot⟧; ⟦b:mēns⟧, ⟦i:mind⟧; ⟦b:ars⟧, ⟦i:art⟧; ⟦b:gēns⟧, ⟦i:tribe⟧; and some others.
⟦i:B. Neuter⟧ ⟦b:ĭ⟧⟦i:-Stems.⟧
These end in the Nominative Singular in ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦b:-al⟧, and ⟦b:-ar⟧. They always have ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the Ablative Singular, ⟦b:-ia⟧ in the Nominative, Accusative, and Vocative Plural, and ⟦b:-ium⟧ in the Genitive Plural, thus holding more steadfastly to the ⟦b:i⟧-character than do Masculine and Feminine ⟦b:ĭ⟧-Stems.
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Sedile⟧, ⟦i:seat⟧; stem, ⟦b:sedīli-⟧.  ⟦b:Animal⟧, ⟦i:animal⟧; stem, ⟦b:animāli-⟧.  ⟦b:Calcar⟧, ⟦i:spur⟧; stem, ⟦b:calcāri-⟧.
SINGULAR.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  TERMINATION.

⟦i:Gen.⟧  sedīl⟦b:is⟧  animāl⟦b:is⟧  calcār⟦b:is⟧  ⟦b:-is⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ī⟧  animāl⟦b:ī⟧  calcār⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  sedīl⟦b:e⟧  animal  calcar  ⟦b:-e⟧ or wanting
⟦i:Voc.⟧  sedīl⟦b:e⟧  animal  calcar  ⟦b:-e⟧ or wanting
⟦i:Abl.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ī⟧  animāl⟦b:ī⟧  calcār⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:-ī⟧
PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ia⟧  animāl⟦b:ia⟧  calcār⟦b:ia⟧  ⟦b:-ia⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ium⟧  animāl⟦b:ium⟧  calcār⟦b:ium⟧  ⟦b:-ium⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ibus⟧  animāl⟦b:ibus⟧  calcār⟦b:ibus⟧  ⟦b:-ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ia⟧  animāl⟦b:ia⟧  calcār⟦b:ia⟧  ⟦b:-ia⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ia⟧  animāl⟦b:ia⟧  calcār⟦b:ia⟧  ⟦b:-ia⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  sedīl⟦b:ibus⟧  animāl⟦b:ibus⟧  calcār⟦b:ibus⟧  ⟦b:-ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
1. In most words of this class the final ⟦b:-i⟧ of the stem is lost in the Nominative Singular; in others it appears as ⟦b:-e⟧.
2. Proper names in ⟦b:-e⟧ form the Ablative Singular in ⟦b:-e⟧; as, ⟦b:Sōracte⟧, ⟦i:Mt. Soracte⟧; so also sometimes ⟦b:mare⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧.
III. Consonant-Stems that have partially adapted themselves to the Inflection of ⟦i:ĭ⟧-Stems.
Many Consonant-Stems have so far adapted themselves to the inflection of ⟦b:ĭ⟧-stems as to take ⟦b:-ium⟧ in the Genitive Plural, and ⟦b:-īs⟧ in the Accusative Plural. Their true character as Consonant-Stems, however, is shown by the fact that they never take ⟦b:-im⟧ in the Accusative Singular, or ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the Ablative Singular. The following words are examples of this class:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Caedēs⟧, f., ⟦i:slaughter⟧; stem, ⟦b:caed-⟧.  ⟦b:Arx⟧, f., ⟦i:citadel⟧; stem, ⟦b:arc-⟧.  ⟦b:Linter⟧, f., ⟦i:skiff⟧; stem, ⟦b:lintr-⟧.

⟦i:a⟧) Nouns in ⟦b:-ēs⟧, with Genitive in ⟦b:-is⟧; as, ⟦b:nūbēs⟧, ⟦b:aedēs⟧, ⟦b:clādēs⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧

⟦i:c⟧) Most nouns in ⟦b:-ns⟧ and ⟦b:-rs⟧ as, ⟦b:cliēns⟧, ⟦b:cohors⟧.
⟦i:d⟧) ⟦b:Ūter⟧, ⟦b:venter⟧; ⟦b:fūr⟧, ⟦b:līs⟧, ⟦b:mās⟧, ⟦b:mūs⟧, ⟦b:nix⟧; and the Plurals ⟦b:faucēs⟧, ⟦b:penātēs⟧, ⟦b:Optimātēs⟧, ⟦b:Samnitēs⟧, ⟦b:Quirītēs⟧.
⟦i:e⟧) Sometimes nouns in ⟦b:-tās⟧ with Genitive ⟦b:-tātis⟧; as, ⟦b:cīvitās⟧, ⟦b:aetās⟧. ⟦b:Cīvitās⟧ ⟦i:usually⟧ has ⟦b:cīvitātium⟧.
IV. Stems in ⟦i:-ī⟧, ⟦i:-ū⟧, and Diphthongs.

3. ⟦b:Juppiter⟧ is for ⟦b:Jou-pater⟧, and therefore contains the same stem as in ⟦b:Jov-is⟧, ⟦b:Jov-ī⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧
⟦b:Nāvis⟧ was originally a diphthong stem ending in ⟦b:au-⟧, but it has passed over to the ⟦b:ĭ⟧-stems (§ 37). Its ablative often ends in ⟦b:-ī⟧.

1. ⟦b:Iter⟧, ⟦b:itineris⟧, n., ⟦i:way⟧, is inflected regularly throughout from the stem ⟦b:itiner-⟧.
2. ⟦b:Supellex⟧, ⟦b:supellectilis⟧, f., ⟦i:furniture⟧, is confined to the Singular. The oblique cases are formed from the stem ⟦b:supellectil-⟧. The ablative has both ⟦b:-ī⟧ and ⟦b:-e⟧.
3. ⟦b:Jecur⟧, n., ⟦i:liver⟧, forms its oblique cases from two stems,—⟦b:jecor-⟧ and ⟦b:jecinor-⟧. Thus, Gen. ⟦b:jecoris⟧ or ⟦b:jecinoris⟧.
4. ⟦b:Femur⟧, n., ⟦i:thigh⟧, usually forms its oblique cases from the stem ⟦b:femor-⟧, but sometimes from the stem ⟦b:femin-⟧. Thus, Gen. ⟦b:femoris⟧ or ⟦b:feminis⟧.
General Principles of Gender in the Third Declension.
1. Nouns in ⟦b:-ō⟧, ⟦b:-or⟧, ⟦b:-ōs⟧, ⟦b:-er⟧, ⟦b:-ĕs⟧ are Masculine.
2. Nouns in ⟦b:-ās⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:-ys⟧, ⟦b:-x⟧, ⟦b:-s⟧ (preceded by a consonant); ⟦b:-dō⟧, ⟦b:-gō⟧ (Genitive ⟦b:-inis⟧); ⟦b:-iō⟧ (abstract and collective), ⟦b:-ūs⟧ (Genitive ⟦b:-ātis⟧ or ⟦b:-ūdis)⟧ are Feminine.
3. Nouns ending in ⟦b:-a⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦b:-i⟧, ⟦b:-y⟧, ⟦b:-o⟧, ⟦b:-l⟧, ⟦b:-n⟧, ⟦b:-t⟧, ⟦b:-ar⟧, ⟦b:-ur⟧, ⟦b:-ŭs⟧ are Neuter.
Chief Exceptions to Gender in the Third Declension.
⟦b:Exceptions to the Rule for Masculines.⟧
1. Nouns in ⟦b:-ō⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Feminine: ⟦b:carō⟧, ⟦i:flesh⟧.
2. Nouns in ⟦b:-or⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Feminine: ⟦b:arbor⟧, ⟦i:tree⟧.
⟦i:b⟧. Neuter: ⟦b:aequor⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧; ⟦b:cor⟧, ⟦i:heart⟧; ⟦b:marmor⟧, ⟦i:marble⟧.
3. Nouns in ⟦b:-ōs⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Feminine: ⟦b:dōs⟧, ⟦i:dowry⟧.
⟦i:b⟧. Neuter: ⟦b:ōs (ōris)⟧, ⟦i:mouth⟧.
4. Nouns in ⟦b:-er⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Feminine: ⟦b:linter⟧, ⟦i:skiff⟧.
⟦i:b⟧. Neuter: ⟦b:cadāver⟧, ⟦i:corpse⟧; ⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦i:way⟧; ⟦b:tūber⟧, ⟦i:tumor⟧; ⟦b:ūber⟧, ⟦i:udder⟧. Also botanical names in ⟦b:-er⟧; as, ⟦b:acer⟧, ⟦i:maple⟧.
5. Nouns in ⟦b:-ĕs⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Feminine: ⟦b:seges⟧, ⟦i:crop⟧.
⟦b:Exceptions to the Rule for Feminines.⟧
1. Nouns in ⟦b:-ās⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:vās⟧, ⟦i:bondsman⟧.
⟦i:b⟧. Neuter: ⟦b:vās⟧, ⟦i:vessel⟧.
2. Nouns in ⟦b:-ēs⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:ariēs⟧, ⟦i:ram⟧; ⟦b:pariēs⟧, ⟦i:wall⟧; ⟦b:pēs⟧, ⟦i:foot⟧.
3. Nouns in ⟦b:-is⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: all nouns in ⟦b:-nis⟧ and ⟦b:-guis⟧; as, ⟦b:amnis⟧, ⟦i:river⟧; ⟦b:īgnis⟧, ⟦i:fire⟧; ⟦b:pānis⟧, ⟦i:bread⟧; ⟦b:sanguis⟧, ⟦i:blood⟧; ⟦b:unguis⟧, ⟦i:nail⟧.
Also—
⟦b:axis⟧, ⟦i:axle⟧. ⟦b:collis⟧, ⟦i:hill⟧. ⟦b:fascis⟧, ⟦i:bundle⟧. ⟦b:lapis⟧, ⟦i:stone⟧. ⟦b:mēnsis⟧, ⟦i:month⟧.  ⟦b:piscis⟧, ⟦i:fish⟧. ⟦b:postis⟧, ⟦i:post⟧. ⟦b:pulvis⟧, ⟦i:dust⟧. ⟦b:orbis⟧, ⟦i:circle⟧. ⟦b:sentis⟧, ⟦i:brier⟧.
⟦/⟧
4. Nouns in ⟦b:-x⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:apex⟧, ⟦i:peak⟧; ⟦b:cōdex⟧, ⟦i:tree-trunk⟧; ⟦b:grex⟧, ⟦i:flock⟧; ⟦b:imbrex⟧, ⟦i:tile⟧; ⟦b:pollex⟧, ⟦i:thumb⟧; ⟦b:vertex⟧, ⟦i:summit⟧; ⟦b:calix⟧, ⟦i:cup⟧.
5. Nouns in ⟦b:-s⟧ preceded by a consonant.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:dēns⟧, ⟦i:tooth⟧; ⟦b:fōns⟧, ⟦i:fountain⟧; ⟦b:mōns⟧, ⟦i:mountain⟧; ⟦b:pōns⟧, ⟦i:bridge⟧.
6. Nouns in ⟦b:-dō⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:cardō⟧, ⟦i:hinge⟧; ⟦b:ōrdō⟧, ⟦i:order⟧.
⟦b:Exceptions to the Rule for Neuters.⟧
1. Nouns in ⟦b:-l⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:sōl⟧, ⟦i:sun⟧; ⟦b:sāl⟧, ⟦i:salt⟧.
2. Nouns in ⟦b:-n⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:pecten⟧, ⟦i:comb⟧.
3. Nouns in ⟦b:-ur⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:vultur⟧, ⟦i:vulture⟧.
4. Nouns in ⟦b:-ŭs⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Masculine: ⟦b:lepus⟧, ⟦i:hare⟧.
Greek Nouns of the Third Declension.
The following are the chief peculiarities of these:—
1. The ending ⟦b:-ă⟧ in the Accusative Singular; as, ⟦b:aetheră⟧, ⟦i:aether⟧; ⟦b:Salamīnă⟧, ⟦i:Salamis⟧.
2. The ending ⟦b:-ĕs⟧ in the Nominative Plural; as, ⟦b:Phrygĕs⟧, ⟦i:Phrygians⟧.
3. The ending ⟦b:-ăs⟧ in the Accusative Plural; as, ⟦b:Phrygăs⟧, ⟦i:Phrygians⟧.
4. Proper names in ⟦b:-ās⟧ (Genitive ⟦b:-antis⟧) have ⟦b:-ā⟧ in the Vocative Singular; as, ⟦b:Atlās (Atlantis)⟧, Vocative ⟦b:Atlā⟧, ⟦i:Atlas⟧.
5. Neuters in ⟦b:-ma⟧ (Genitive ⟦b:-matis⟧) have ⟦b:-īs⟧ instead of ⟦b:-ibus⟧ in the Dative and Ablative Plural; as, ⟦b:poēmatīs⟧, ⟦i:poems⟧.
6. ⟦b:Orpheus⟧, and other proper names ending in ⟦b:-eus⟧, form the Vocative Singular in ⟦b:-eu (Orpheu⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧). But in prose the other cases usually follow the second declension; as, ⟦b:Orpheī⟧, ⟦b:Orpheō⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧
7. Proper names in ⟦b:-ēs⟧, like ⟦b:Periclēs⟧, form the Genitive Singular sometimes in ⟦b:-is⟧, sometimes in ⟦b:-ī⟧, as, ⟦b:Periclis⟧ or ⟦b:Periclī⟧.
8. Feminine proper names in ⟦b:-ō⟧ have ⟦b:-ūs⟧ in the Genitive, but ⟦b:-ō⟧ in the other oblique cases; as,—
⟦i:Nom.⟧  Didō  ⟦i:Acc.⟧  Didō
⟦i:Gen.⟧  Didūs  ⟦i:Voc.⟧  Didō
⟦i:Dat.⟧  Didō  ⟦i:Abl.⟧  Didō
⟦/⟧
9. The regular Latin endings often occur in Greek nouns.
⟦i:ŭ⟧-Stems.

title: Fourth Declension
text:
Nouns of the Fourth Declension end in ⟦b:-us⟧ Masculine, and ⟦b:-ū⟧ Neuter. They are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Frūctus⟧, m., ⟦i:fruit⟧.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Cornū⟧, n., ⟦i:horn⟧.
⟦.⟧  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  frūct⟦b:us⟧  frūct⟦b:ūs⟧  corn⟦b:ū⟧  corn⟦b:ua⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  frūct⟦b:ūs⟧  frūct⟦b:uum⟧  corn⟦b:ūs⟧  corn⟦b:uum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  frūct⟦b:uī⟧  frūct⟦b:ibus⟧  corn⟦b:ū⟧  corn⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  frūct⟦b:um⟧  frūct⟦b:ūs⟧  corn⟦b:ū⟧  corn⟦b:ua⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  frūct⟦b:us⟧  frūct⟦b:ūs⟧  corn⟦b:ū⟧  corn⟦b:ua⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  frūct⟦b:ū⟧  frūct⟦b:ibus⟧  corn⟦b:ū⟧  corn⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
Peculiarities of Nouns of the Fourth Declension.
1. Nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧, particularly in early Latin, often form the Genitive Singular in ⟦b:-ī⟧, following the analogy of nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧ of the Second Declension; as, ⟦b:senātī⟧, ⟦b:ōrnātī⟧. This is usually the case in Plautus and Terence.
2. Nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧ sometimes have ⟦b:-ū⟧ in the Dative Singular, instead of ⟦b:-uī⟧; as, ⟦b:frūctū⟧ (for ⟦b:frūctuī⟧).
3. The ending ⟦b:-ubus⟧, instead of ⟦b:-ibus⟧, occurs in the Dative and Ablative Plural of ⟦b:artūs⟧ (Plural), ⟦i:limbs⟧; ⟦b:tribus⟧, ⟦i:tribe⟧; and in dis-syllables in ⟦b:-cus⟧; as, ⟦b:artubus⟧, ⟦b:tribubus⟧, ⟦b:arcubus⟧, ⟦b:lacubus⟧. But with the exception of ⟦b:tribus⟧, all these words admit the forms in ⟦b:-ibus⟧ as well as those in ⟦b:-ubus⟧.
4. ⟦b:Domus⟧, ⟦i:house⟧, is declined according to the Fourth Declension, but has also the following forms of the Second:—
⟦b:domī⟧ (locative), ⟦i:at home⟧;
⟦b:domō⟧, ⟦i:from home⟧;
⟦b:domum⟧, ⟦i:homewards⟧, ⟦i:to one's home⟧;
⟦b:domōs⟧, ⟦i:homewards⟧, ⟦i:to their⟧ (⟦i:etc.⟧) ⟦i:homes⟧
5. The only Neuters of this declension in common use are: ⟦b:cornū⟧, ⟦i:horn⟧; ⟦b:genū⟧, ⟦i:knee⟧; and ⟦b:verū⟧, ⟦i:spit⟧.
Exceptions to Gender in the Fourth Declension.
The following nouns in ⟦b:-us⟧ are Feminine: ⟦b:acus⟧, ⟦i:needle⟧; ⟦b:domus⟧, ⟦i:house⟧; ⟦b:manus⟧, ⟦i:hand⟧; ⟦b:porticus⟧, ⟦i:colonnade⟧; ⟦b:tribus⟧, ⟦i:tribe⟧; ⟦b:Īdūs⟧ (Plural), ⟦i:Ides⟧; also names of trees (§ 15, 2).
ē-Stems.

title: Fifth Declension
text:
Nouns of the Fifth Declension end in ⟦b:-ēs⟧, and are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Diēs⟧, m., ⟦i:day⟧.  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Rēs⟧, f., ⟦i:thing⟧.
⟦.⟧  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.  SINGULAR.  PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  di⟦b:ēs⟧  di⟦b:ēs⟧  r⟦b:ēs⟧  r⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  di⟦b:ēī⟧  di⟦b:ērum⟧  r⟦b:ĕī⟧  r⟦b:ērum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  di⟦b:ēī⟧  di⟦b:ēbus⟧  r⟦b:ĕī⟧  r⟦b:ēbus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  di⟦b:em⟧  di⟦b:ēs⟧  r⟦b:em⟧  r⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  di⟦b:ēs⟧  di⟦b:ēs⟧  r⟦b:ēs⟧  r⟦b:ēs⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  di⟦b:ē⟧  di⟦b:ēbus⟧  r⟦b:ē⟧  r⟦b:ēbus⟧
⟦/⟧
Peculiarities of Nouns of the Fifth Declension.
1. The ending of the Genitive and Dative Singular is ⟦b:-ĕī⟧, instead of ⟦b:-ēī⟧, when a consonant precedes; as, ⟦b:spĕī⟧, ⟦b:rĕī⟧, ⟦b:fidĕī⟧.
2. A Genitive ending ⟦b:-ī⟧ (for ⟦b:-ĕī⟧) is found in ⟦b:plēbī⟧ (from ⟦b:plēbēs⟧ = ⟦b:plēbs⟧) in the expressions ⟦b:tribūnus plēbī⟧, ⟦i:tribune of the people⟧, and ⟦b:plēbī scītum⟧, ⟦i:decree of the people⟧; sometimes also in other words.
3. A Genitive and Dative form in ⟦b:-ē⟧ sometimes occurs; as, ⟦b:aciē⟧.
4. With the exception of ⟦b:diēs⟧ and ⟦b:rēs⟧, most nouns of the Fifth Declension are not declined in the Plural. But ⟦b:aciēs⟧, ⟦b:seriēs⟧, ⟦b:speciēs⟧, ⟦b:spēs⟧, and a few others are used in the Nominative and Accusative Plural.
Gender in the Fifth Declension.
Nouns of the Fifth Declension are regularly Feminine, except ⟦b:diēs⟧, ⟦i:day⟧, and ⟦b:merīdiēs⟧, ⟦i:mid-day⟧. But ⟦b:diēs⟧ is sometimes Feminine in the Singular, particularly when it means an ⟦i:appointed day⟧.

title: Defective Nouns
text:
Here belong—
1. Nouns used in the Singular only.
2. Nouns used in the Plural only.
3. Nouns used only in certain cases.
4. Indeclinable Nouns.
Nouns used in the Singular only.
Many nouns, from the nature of their signification, are regularly used in the Singular only. Thus:—
1. ⟦b:Proper names⟧; as, ⟦b:Cicerō⟧, ⟦i:Cicero⟧; ⟦b:Italia⟧, ⟦i:Italy⟧.
2. ⟦b:Nouns denoting material⟧; as, ⟦b:aes⟧, ⟦i:copper⟧; ⟦b:lac⟧, ⟦i:milk⟧.
3. ⟦b:Abstract nouns⟧; as, ⟦b:ignōrantia⟧, ⟦i:ignorance⟧; ⟦b:bonitās⟧, ⟦i:goodness⟧.
4. But the above classes of words are sometimes used in the Plural. Thus:—
⟦i:a⟧) Proper names,—to denote different members of a family, or specimens of a type; as, ⟦b:Cicerōnēs⟧, ⟦i:the Ciceros⟧; ⟦b:Catōnēs⟧, ⟦i:men like Cato⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) Names of materials,—to denote objects made of the material, or different kinds of the substance; as, ⟦b:aera⟧, ⟦i:bronzes⟧ (⟦i:i.e.⟧ bronze figures); ⟦b:ligna⟧, ⟦i:woods⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) Abstract nouns,—to denote instances of the quality; as, ⟦b:ignōrantiae⟧, ⟦i:cases of ignorance⟧.
Nouns used in the Plural only.
Here belong—
1. Many geographical names; as, ⟦b:Thēbae⟧, ⟦i:Thebes⟧; ⟦b:Leuctra⟧, ⟦i:Leuctra⟧; ⟦b:Pompejī⟧, ⟦i:Pompeii⟧.
2. Many names of festivals; as, ⟦b:Megalēsia⟧, ⟦i:the Megalesian festival⟧.
3. Many special words, of which the following are the most important:—
⟦b:angustiae⟧, ⟦i:narrow pass⟧. ⟦b:arma⟧, ⟦i:weapons⟧. ⟦b:dēliciae⟧, ⟦i:delight⟧. ⟦b:dīvitiae⟧, ⟦i:riches⟧. ⟦b:Īdūs⟧, ⟦i:Ides⟧. ⟦b:indūtiae⟧, ⟦i:truce⟧. ⟦b:īnsidiae⟧, ⟦i:ambush⟧. ⟦b:majōrēs⟧, ⟦i:ancestors⟧.  ⟦b:mānēs⟧, ⟦i:spirits of the dead⟧. ⟦b:moenia⟧, ⟦i:city walls⟧. ⟦b:minae⟧, ⟦i:threats⟧. ⟦b:nūptiae⟧, ⟦i:marriage⟧. ⟦b:posterī⟧, ⟦i:descendants⟧. ⟦b:reliquiae⟧, ⟦i:remainder⟧. ⟦b:tenebrae⟧, ⟦i:darkness⟧. ⟦b:verbera⟧, ⟦i:blows⟧.
⟦/⟧
Also in classical prose regularly—
⟦b:cervīcēs⟧, ⟦i:neck⟧. ⟦b:fidēs⟧, ⟦i:lyre⟧.  ⟦b:nārēs⟧, ⟦i:nose⟧. ⟦b:vīscerā⟧, ⟦i:viscera⟧.
⟦/⟧
Nouns used only in Certain Cases.
1. ⟦b:Used in only One Case.⟧ Many nouns of the Fourth Declension are found only in the Ablative Singular as, ⟦b:jussū⟧, ⟦i:by the order⟧; ⟦b:injussū⟧, ⟦i:without the order⟧; ⟦b:nātū⟧, ⟦i:by birth⟧.
2. ⟦b:Used in Two Cases.⟧
⟦i:a⟧. ⟦b:Fors⟧ (⟦i:chance⟧), Nom. Sing.; ⟦b:forte⟧, Abl. Sing.
⟦i:b⟧. ⟦b:Spontis⟧ (⟦i:free-will⟧), Gen. Sing.; ⟦b:sponte⟧, Abl. Sing.
3. ⟦b:Used in Three Cases. Nēmō⟧, ⟦i:no one⟧ (Nom.), has also the Dat. ⟦b:nēminī⟧ and the Acc. ⟦b:nēminem⟧. The Gen. and Abl. are supplied by the corresponding cases of ⟦b:nūllus⟧; ⟦i:viz.⟧ ⟦b:nūllīus⟧ and ⟦b:nūllō⟧.
4. ⟦b:Impetus⟧ has the Nom., Acc., and Abl. Sing., and the Nom. and Acc. Plu.; ⟦i:viz.⟧ ⟦b:impetus⟧, ⟦b:impetum⟧, ⟦b:impetū⟧, ⟦b:impetūs⟧.
5.
⟦i:a⟧. ⟦b:Precī⟧, ⟦b:precem⟧, ⟦b:prece⟧, lacks the Nom. and Gen. Sing.
⟦i:b⟧. ⟦b:Vicis⟧, ⟦b:vicem⟧, ⟦b:vice⟧, lacks the Nom. and Dat. Sing.
6. ⟦b:Opis⟧, ⟦b:dapis⟧, and ⟦b:frūgis⟧,—all lack the Nom. Sing.
7. Many monosyllables of the Third Declension lack the Gen. Plu.: ⟦b:as⟧, ⟦b:cor⟧, ⟦b:lūx⟧, ⟦b:sōl⟧, ⟦b:aes⟧, ⟦b:ōs⟧ (⟦b:ōris⟧), ⟦b:rūs⟧, ⟦b:sāl⟧, ⟦b:tūs⟧.
Indeclinable Nouns.
Here belong—
⟦b:fās⟧, n., ⟦i:right⟧. ⟦b:īnstar⟧, n., ⟦i:likeness⟧. ⟦b:māne⟧, n., ⟦i:morning⟧.  ⟦b:nefās⟧, n., ⟦i:impiety⟧. ⟦b:nihil⟧, n., ⟦i:nothing⟧. ⟦b:secus⟧, n., ⟦i:sex⟧.
⟦/⟧
1. With the exception of ⟦b:māne⟧ (which may serve also as Ablative, ⟦i:in the morning⟧), the nouns in this list are simply Neuters confined in use to the Nominative and Accusative Singular.
Heteroclites.
These are nouns whose forms are partly of one declension, and partly of another. Thus:—
1. Several nouns have the entire Singular of one declension, while the Plural is of another; as,—
⟦b:vās⟧, ⟦b:vāsis⟧ (⟦i:vessel⟧);  Plu., ⟦b:vāsa⟧, ⟦b:vāsorōum⟧, ⟦b:vāsīs⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧
⟦b:jūgerum⟧, ⟦b:jūgerī⟧ (⟦i:acre⟧);  Plu., ⟦b:jūgera⟧, ⟦b:jūgerum⟧, ⟦b:jūgeribus⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧
⟦/⟧
2. Several nouns, while belonging in the main to one declension, have certain special forms belonging to another. Thus:—
⟦i:a⟧) Many nouns of the First Declension ending in ⟦b:-ia⟧ take also a Nom. and Acc. of the Fifth; as, ⟦b:māteriēs⟧, ⟦b:māteriem⟧, ⟦i:material⟧, as well as ⟦b:māteria⟧, ⟦b:māteriam⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) ⟦b:Famēs⟧, ⟦i:hunger⟧, regularly of the Third Declension, has the Abl. ⟦b:famē⟧ of the Fifth.
⟦i:c⟧) ⟦b:Requiēs⟧, ⟦b:requiētis⟧, ⟦i:rest⟧, regularly of the Third Declension, takes an Acc. of the Fifth, ⟦b:requiem⟧, in addition to ⟦b:requiētem⟧.
⟦i:d⟧) Besides ⟦b:plēbs⟧, ⟦b:plēbis⟧, ⟦i:common people⟧, of the Third Declension, we find ⟦b:plēbēs⟧, ⟦b:plēbĕī⟧ (also ⟦b:plēbī⟧, see § 52, 2), of the Fifth.
Heterogeneous Nouns.
Heterogeneous nouns vary in Gender. Thus:—
1. Several nouns of the Second Declension have two forms,—one Masc. in ⟦b:-us⟧, and one Neuter in ⟦b:-um⟧; as, ⟦b:clipeus⟧, ⟦b:clipeum⟧, ⟦i:shield⟧; ⟦b:carrus⟧, ⟦b:carrum⟧, ⟦i:cart⟧.
2. Other nouns have one gender in the Singular, another in the Plural; as,—
SINGULAR.  PLURAL.
⟦b:balneum⟧, n., ⟦i:bath⟧;  ⟦b:balneae⟧, f., ⟦i:bath-house⟧.
⟦b:epulum⟧, n., ⟦i:feast⟧;  ⟦b:epulae⟧, f., ⟦i:feast⟧.
⟦b:frēnum⟧, n., ⟦i:bridle⟧;  ⟦b:frēnī⟧, m.(rarely ⟦b:frēna⟧, n.), ⟦i:bridle⟧.
⟦b:jocus⟧, m., ⟦i:jest⟧;  ⟦b:joca⟧, n. (also ⟦b:jocī⟧, m.), ⟦i:jests⟧.
⟦b:locus⟧, m., ⟦i:place⟧;  ⟦b:loca⟧, n., ⟦i:places⟧; ⟦b:locī⟧, m., ⟦i:passages or topics in an author⟧.
⟦b:rāstrum⟧, n., ⟦i:rake⟧;  ⟦b:rāstrī⟧, m.; ⟦b:rāstra⟧, n., ⟦i:rakes⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. Heterogeneous nouns may at the same time be heteroclites, as in case of the first two examples above.
Plurals with Change of Meaning.
The following nouns have one meaning in the Singular, and another in the Plural:—
SINGULAR.  PLURAL.
⟦b:aedēs⟧, ⟦i:temple⟧;  ⟦b:aedēs⟧, ⟦i:house⟧.
⟦b:auxilium⟧, ⟦i:help⟧;  ⟦b:auxilia⟧, ⟦i:auxiliary troops⟧.
⟦b:carcer⟧, ⟦i:prison⟧;  ⟦b:carcerēs⟧, ⟦i:stalls for racing-chariot⟧.
⟦b:castrum⟧, ⟦i:fort⟧;  ⟦b:castra⟧, ⟦i:camp⟧.
⟦b:cōpia⟧, ⟦i:abundance⟧;  ⟦b:cōpiae⟧, ⟦i:troops⟧, ⟦i:resources⟧.
⟦b:fīnis⟧, ⟦i:end⟧;  ⟦b:fīnēs⟧, ⟦i:borders⟧, ⟦i:territory⟧.
⟦b:fortūna⟧, ⟦i:fortune⟧;  ⟦b:fortūnae⟧, ⟦i:possessions⟧, ⟦i:wealth⟧.
⟦b:grātia⟧, ⟦i:favor⟧, ⟦i:gratitude⟧;  ⟦b:grātiae⟧, ⟦i:thanks⟧.
⟦b:impedīmentum⟧, ⟦i:hindrance⟧;  ⟦b:impedīmenta⟧, ⟦i:baggage⟧.
⟦b:littera⟧, ⟦i:letter⟧ (of the alphabet);  ⟦b:litterae⟧, ⟦i:epistle; literature⟧.
⟦b:mōs⟧, ⟦i:habit⟧, ⟦i:custom⟧;  ⟦b:mōrēs⟧, ⟦i:character⟧.
⟦b:opera⟧, ⟦i:help⟧, ⟦i:service⟧;  ⟦b:operae⟧, ⟦i:laborers⟧.
(⟦b:ops⟧) ⟦b:opis⟧, ⟦i:help⟧;  ⟦b:opēs⟧, ⟦i:resources⟧.
⟦b:pars⟧, ⟦i:part⟧;  ⟦b:partēs⟧, ⟦i:party⟧; ⟦i:rôle⟧.
⟦b:sāl⟧, ⟦i:salt⟧;  ⟦b:sălēs⟧, ⟦i:wit⟧.
⟦/⟧

title: Adjectives of the First and Second Declensions
text:
In these the Masculine is declined like ⟦b:hortus⟧, ⟦b:puer⟧, or ⟦b:ager⟧, the Feminine like ⟦b:porta⟧, and the Neuter like ⟦b:bellum⟧. Thus, Masculine like ⟦b:hortus:—⟧
⟦=⟧⟦b:Bonus⟧, ⟦i:good⟧.  SINGULAR.
⟦.⟧  MASCULINE.  FEMININE.  NEUTER.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  bon⟦b:us⟧  bon⟦b:a⟧  bon⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  bon⟦b:ī⟧  bon⟦b:ae⟧  bon⟦b:ī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  bon⟦b:ō⟧  bon⟦b:ae⟧  bon⟦b:ō⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  bon⟦b:um⟧  bon⟦b:am⟧  bon⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  bon⟦b:e⟧  bon⟦b:a⟧  bon⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  bon⟦b:ō⟧  bon⟦b:ā⟧  bon⟦b:ō⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  bon⟦b:ī⟧  bon⟦b:ae⟧  bon⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  bon⟦b:ōrum⟧  bon⟦b:ārum⟧  bon⟦b:ōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  bon⟦b:īs⟧  bon⟦b:īs⟧  bon⟦b:īs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  bon⟦b:ōs⟧  bon⟦b:ās⟧  bon⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  bon⟦b:ī⟧  bon⟦b:ae⟧  bon⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  bon⟦b:īs⟧  bon⟦b:īs⟧  bon⟦b:īs⟧
⟦/⟧
1. The Gen. Sing. Masc. and Neut. of Adjectives in ⟦b:-ius⟧ ends in ⟦b:-iī⟧ (not in ⟦b:-ī⟧ as in case of Nouns; see § 25, 1; 2). So also the Voc. Sing. of such Adjectives ends in ⟦b:-ie⟧, not in ⟦b:ī⟧. Thus ⟦b:eximius⟧ forms Gen. ⟦b:eximiī⟧; Voc. ⟦b:eximie⟧.
2. Distributives (see § 78, 1, ⟦i:c⟧) regularly form the Gen. Plu. Masc. and Neut. in ⟦b:-um⟧ instead of ⟦b:-ōrum⟧ (compare § 25, 6); as, ⟦b:dēnum centēnum⟧; but always ⟦b:singulōrum⟧.
Masculine like ⟦b:puer:—⟧
⟦=⟧⟦b:Tener⟧, ⟦i:tender⟧.  SINGULAR.
⟦.⟧  MASCULINE.  FEMININE  NEUTER.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  tener  tener⟦b:a⟧  tener⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  tener⟦b:ī⟧  tener⟦b:ae⟧  tener⟦b:ī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  tener⟦b:ō⟧  tener⟦b:ae⟧  tener⟦b:ō⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  tener⟦b:um⟧  tener⟦b:am⟧  tener⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  tener  tener⟦b:a⟧  tener⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  tener⟦b:ō⟧  tener⟦b:ā⟧  tener⟦b:ō⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  tener⟦b:ī⟧  tener⟦b:ae⟧  tener⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  tener⟦b:ōrum⟧  tener⟦b:ārum⟧  tener⟦b:ōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  tener⟦b:īs⟧  tener⟦b:īs⟧  tener⟦b:īs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  tener⟦b:ōs⟧  tener⟦b:ās⟧  tener⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  tener⟦b:ī⟧  tener⟦b:ae⟧  tener⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  tener⟦b:īs⟧  tener⟦b:īs⟧  tener⟦b:īs⟧
⟦/⟧
Masculine like ⟦b:ager:—⟧
⟦=⟧⟦b:Sacer⟧, ⟦i:sacred⟧.  SINGULAR.
⟦.⟧  MASCULINE.  FEMININE.  NEUTER.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  sacer  sacr⟦b:a⟧  sacr⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  sacr⟦b:ī⟧  sacr⟦b:ae⟧  sacr⟦b:ī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  sacr⟦b:ō⟧  sacr⟦b:ae⟧  sacr⟦b:ō⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  sacr⟦b:um⟧  sacr⟦b:am⟧  sacr⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  sacer  sacr⟦b:a⟧  sacr⟦b:um⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  sacr⟦b:ō⟧  sacr⟦b:ā⟧  sacr⟦b:ō⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  sacr⟦b:ī⟧  sacr⟦b:ae⟧  sacr⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  sacr⟦b:ōrum⟧  sacr⟦b:ārum⟧  sacr⟦b:ōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  sacr⟦b:īs⟧  sacr⟦b:īs⟧  sacr⟦b:īs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  sacr⟦b:ōs⟧  sacr⟦b:ās⟧  sacr⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  sacr⟦b:ī⟧  sacr⟦b:ae⟧  sacr⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  sacr⟦b:īs⟧  sacr⟦b:īs⟧  sacr⟦b:īs⟧
⟦/⟧
1. Most adjectives in ⟦b:-er⟧ are declined like ⟦b:sacer⟧. The following however, are declined like ⟦b:tener⟧: ⟦b:asper⟧, ⟦i:rough⟧; ⟦b:lacer⟧, ⟦i:torn⟧; ⟦b:līber⟧, ⟦i:free⟧; ⟦b:miser⟧, ⟦i:wretched⟧; ⟦b:prōsper⟧, ⟦i:prosperous⟧; compounds in ⟦b:-fer⟧ and ⟦b:-ger⟧; sometimes ⟦b:dexter⟧, ⟦i:right⟧.
2. ⟦b:Satur⟧, ⟦i:full⟧, is declined: ⟦b:satur⟧, ⟦b:satura⟧, ⟦b:saturum⟧.
Nine Irregular Adjectives.
Here belong—
⟦b:alius⟧, ⟦i:another⟧;  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:alter⟧, ⟦i:the other⟧;
⟦b:ūllus⟧, ⟦i:any⟧;  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:nūllus⟧, ⟦i:none⟧;
⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦i:which?⟧ (of two);  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:neuter⟧, ⟦i:neither⟧;
⟦b:sōlus⟧, ⟦i:alone⟧;  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:tōtus⟧, ⟦i:whole⟧;

⟦/⟧
They are declined as follows:—

1. All these words lack the Vocative. The Plural is regular.
2. ⟦b:Neuter⟧ is declined like ⟦b:uter⟧.

title: Adjectives of the Third Declension
text:
These fall into three classes,—
1. Adjectives of three terminations in the Nominative Singular,—one for each gender.
2. Adjectives of two terminations.
3. Adjectives of one termination.
⟦i:a⟧. With the exception of Comparatives, and a few other words mentioned below in § 70, 1, all Adjectives of the Third Declension follow the inflection of ⟦b:ĭ⟧-stems; ⟦i:i.e.⟧ they have the Ablative Singular in ⟦b:-ī⟧, the Genitive Plural in ⟦b:-ium⟧, the Accusative Plural in ⟦b:-īs⟧ (as well as ⟦b:-ēs⟧) in the Masculine and Feminine, and the Nominative and Accusative Plural in ⟦b:-ia⟧ in Neuters.
Adjectives of Three Terminations.
These are declined as follows:—
⟦=⟧⟦b:Ācer⟧, ⟦i:sharp⟧.  SINGULAR.
⟦.⟧  MASCULINE.  FEMININE.  NEUTER.

1. Like ⟦b:ācer⟧ are declined ⟦b:alacer⟧, ⟦i:lively⟧; ⟦b:campester⟧, ⟦i:level⟧; ⟦b:celeber⟧, ⟦i:famous⟧; ⟦b:equester⟧, ⟦i:equestrian⟧; ⟦b:palūster⟧, ⟦i:marshy⟧; ⟦b:pedester⟧, ⟦i:pedestrian⟧; ⟦b:puter⟧, ⟦i:rotten⟧; ⟦b:salūber⟧, ⟦i:wholesome⟧; ⟦b:silvester⟧, ⟦i:woody⟧; ⟦b:terrester⟧, ⟦i:terrestrial⟧; ⟦b:volucer⟧, ⟦i:winged⟧; also names of months in ⟦b:-ber⟧, as ⟦b:September⟧.
2. ⟦b:Celer⟧, ⟦b:celeris⟧, ⟦b:celere⟧, ⟦i:swift⟧, retains the ⟦b:e⟧ before ⟦b:r⟧, but lacks the Genitive Plural.
3. In the Nominative Singular of Adjectives of this class the Feminine form is sometimes used for the Masculine. This is regularly true of ⟦b:salūbris⟧, ⟦b:silvestris⟧, and ⟦b:terrestris⟧. In case of the other words in the list, the use of the Feminine for the Masculine is confined chiefly to early and late Latin, and to poetry.
Adjectives of Two Terminations.
These are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Fortis⟧, ⟦i:strong.⟧  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:Fortior⟧, ⟦i:stronger.⟧

⟦i:Abl.⟧  fort⟦b:ibus⟧  fort⟦b:ibus⟧  fortiōr⟦b:ibus⟧  fortiōr⟦b:ibus⟧

1. ⟦b:Fortior⟧ is the Comparative of ⟦b:fortis⟧. All Comparatives are regularly declined in the same way. The Acc. Plu. in ⟦b:-īs⟧ is rare.

⟦.⟧  M. AND F.  NEUT.  M. AND F.  NEUT.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  vetus  vetus  ——  plūs
⟦i:Gen.⟧  veter⟦b:is⟧  veter⟦b:is⟧  ——  plūr⟦b:is⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  veter⟦b:ī⟧  veter⟦b:ī⟧  ——  ——

⟦i:Voc.⟧  vetus  vetus  ——  ——
⟦i:Abl.⟧  veter⟦b:e⟧  veter⟦b:e⟧  ——  plūr⟦b:e⟧
⟦=⟧PLURAL.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  veter⟦b:ēs⟧  veter⟦b:a⟧  plūr⟦b:ēs⟧  plūr⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  veter⟦b:um⟧  veter⟦b:um⟧  plūr⟦b:ium⟧  plūr⟦b:ium⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  veter⟦b:ibus⟧  veter⟦b:ibus⟧  plūr⟦b:ibus⟧  plūr⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  veter⟦b:ēs⟧  veter⟦b:a⟧  plūr⟦b:ēs⟧, ⟦b:-īs⟧  plūr⟦b:a⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  veter⟦b:ēs⟧  veter⟦b:a⟧  ——  ——
⟦i:Abl.⟧  veter⟦b:ibus⟧  veter⟦b:ibus⟧  plūr⟦b:ibus⟧  plūr⟦b:ibus⟧
⟦/⟧
1. It will be observed that ⟦b:vetus⟧ is declined as a pure Consonant-Stem; ⟦i:i.e.⟧ Ablative Singular in ⟦b:-e⟧, Genitive Plural in ⟦b:-um⟧, Nominative Plural Neuter in ⟦b:-a⟧, and Accusative Plural Masculine and Feminine in ⟦b:-ēs⟧ only. In the same way are declined ⟦b:compos⟧, ⟦i:controlling⟧; ⟦b:dīves⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧; ⟦b:particeps⟧, ⟦i:sharing⟧; ⟦b:pauper⟧, ⟦i:poor⟧; ⟦b:prīnceps⟧, ⟦i:chief⟧; ⟦b:sōspes⟧, ⟦i:safe⟧; ⟦b:superstes⟧, ⟦i:surviving⟧. Yet ⟦b:dīves⟧ always has Neut. Plu. ⟦b:dītia⟧.
2. ⟦b:Inops⟧, ⟦i:needy⟧, and ⟦b:memor⟧, ⟦i:mindful⟧, have Ablative Singular ⟦b:inopī⟧, ⟦b:memorī⟧, but Genitive Plural ⟦b:inopum⟧, ⟦b:memorum⟧.
3. Participles in ⟦b:-āns⟧ and ⟦b:-ēns⟧ follow the declension of ⟦b:ī⟧-stems. But they do not have ⟦b:-ī⟧ the Ablative, except when employed as adjectives; when used as participles or as substantives, they have ⟦b:-e⟧; as,—
⟦b:ā sapientī virō⟧, ⟦i:by a wise man⟧; but
⟦b:ā sapiente⟧, ⟦i:by a philosopher.⟧
⟦b:Tarquiniō rēgnante⟧, ⟦i:under the reign of Tarquin.⟧
4. ⟦b:Plūs⟧, in the Singular, is always a noun.
5. In the Ablative Singular, adjectives, when used as substantives,—
⟦i:a⟧) usually retain the adjective declension; as,—
⟦b:aequālis⟧, ⟦i:contemporary⟧, Abl. ⟦b:aequālī⟧.
⟦b:cōnsulāris⟧, ⟦i:ex-consul⟧, Abl. ⟦b:cōnsulārī⟧
So names of Months; as, ⟦b:Aprīlī⟧, ⟦i:April⟧; ⟦b:Decembrī⟧, ⟦i:December⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) But adjectives used as proper names have ⟦b:-e⟧ in the Ablative Singular; as, ⟦b:Celere⟧, Celer; ⟦b:Juvenāle⟧, ⟦i:Juvenal⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) Patrials in ⟦b:-ās⟧, ⟦b:-ātis⟧ and ⟦b:-īs⟧, ⟦b:-ītis⟧, when designating places regularly have ⟦b:-ī⟧; as, ⟦b:in Arpīnātī⟧, ⟦i:on the estate at Arpinum⟧, yet ⟦b:-e⟧, when used of persons; as, ⟦b:ab Arpīnāte⟧, ⟦i:by an Arpinatian⟧.
6. A very few indeclinable adjectives occur, the chief of which are ⟦b:frūgī⟧, ⟦i:frugal⟧; ⟦b:nēquam⟧, ⟦i:worthless⟧.
7. In poetry, adjectives and participles in ⟦b:-ns⟧ sometimes form the Gen. Plu. in ⟦b:-um⟧ instead of ⟦b:-ium⟧; as, ⟦b:venientum⟧, ⟦i:of those coming⟧.

title: Comparison of Adjectives
text:
1. There are three degrees of Comparison,—the Positive, the Comparative, and the Superlative.
2. The Comparative is regularly formed by adding ⟦b:-ior⟧ (Neut. ⟦b:-ius⟧), and the Superlative by adding ⟦b:-issimus⟧ (⟦b:-a⟧, ⟦b:-um⟧), to the Stem of the Positive deprived of its final vowel; as,—
altus, ⟦i:high⟧,  alt⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:higher⟧,  alt⟦b:issimus⟧, ⟦i:highest⟧, ⟦i:very high⟧.
fortis, ⟦i:brave⟧,  fort⟦b:ior⟧,  fort⟦b:issimus⟧.
fēlīx, ⟦i:fortunate⟧,  fēlīc⟦b:ior⟧,  fēlīc⟦b:issimus⟧.
⟦/⟧
So also Participles, when used as Adjectives; as,—
doctus, ⟦i:learned⟧,  doct⟦b:ior⟧,  doct⟦b:issimus⟧.
egēns, ⟦i:needy⟧,  egent⟦b:ior⟧,  egent⟦b:issimus⟧.
⟦/⟧
3. Adjectives in ⟦b:-er⟧ form the Superlative by appending ⟦b:-rimus⟧ to the Nominative of the Positive. The Comparative is regular. Thus:—
asper, ⟦i:rough⟧,  asper⟦b:ior⟧,  asper⟦b:rimus⟧.
pulcher, ⟦i:beautiful⟧,  pulchr⟦b:ior⟧,  pulcher⟦b:rimus⟧.
ācer, ⟦i:sharp⟧,  ācr⟦b:ior⟧,  ācer⟦b:rimus⟧.
celer, ⟦i:swift⟧,  celer⟦b:ior⟧,  celer⟦b:rimus⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. Notice mātūr⟦b:us⟧, mātūr⟦b:ior⟧, mātūr⟦b:issimus⟧ or mātūr⟦b:rimus⟧.
4. Five Adjectives in ⟦b:-ilis⟧ form the Superlative by adding ⟦b:-limus⟧ to the Stem of the Positive deprived of its final vowel. The Comparative is regular. Thus:—
facilis, ⟦i:easy⟧,  facil⟦b:ior⟧,  facil⟦b:limus⟧.
difficilis, ⟦i:diffcult⟧,  difficil⟦b:ior⟧,  difficil⟦b:limus⟧.
similis, ⟦i:like⟧,  simil⟦b:ior⟧,  simil⟦b:limus⟧.
dissimilis, ⟦i:unlike⟧,  dissimil⟦b:ior⟧,  dissimil⟦b:limus⟧.
humilis, ⟦i:low⟧,  humil⟦b:ior⟧,  humil⟦b:limus⟧.
⟦/⟧
5. Adjectives in ⟦b:-dicus⟧, ⟦b:-ficus⟧, and ⟦b:-volus⟧ form the Comparative and Superlative as though from forms in ⟦b:-dīcēns⟧, ⟦b:-ficēns⟧, ⟦b:-volēns⟧. Thus:—
maledicus, ⟦i:slanderous⟧,  maledīcent⟦b:ior⟧,  maledīcent⟦b:issimus⟧.
magnificus, ⟦i:magnificent⟧,  magnificent⟦b:ior⟧,  magnificent⟦b:issimus⟧.
benevolus, ⟦i:kindly⟧,  benevolent⟦b:ior⟧,  benevolent⟦b:issimus⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. Positives in ⟦b:-dīcēns⟧ and ⟦b:-volēns⟧ occur in early Latin; as ⟦b:maledīcēns⟧, ⟦b:benevolēns⟧.
6. ⟦b:Dīves⟧ has the Comparative ⟦b:dīvitior⟧ or ⟦b:dītior⟧; Superlative ⟦b:dīvitissimus⟧ or ⟦b:dītissimus⟧.
Irregular Comparison.
Several Adjectives vary the Stem in Comparison; ⟦i:viz⟧.—
bonus, ⟦i:good⟧,  mel⟦b:ior⟧,  opt⟦b:imus⟧.
malus, ⟦i:bad⟧,  pe⟦b:jor⟧,  pess⟦b:imus⟧.
parvus, ⟦i:small⟧,  min⟦b:or⟧,  min⟦b:imus⟧.
magnus, ⟦i:large⟧,  ma⟦b:jor⟧,  max⟦b:imus⟧.
multus, ⟦i:much⟧,  plūs,  plūr⟦b:imus⟧,
frūgī, ⟦i:thrifty⟧,  frūgāl⟦b:ior⟧,  frūgāl⟦b:issimus⟧,
nēquam, ⟦i:worthless⟧,  nēqu⟦b:ior⟧,  nēqu⟦b:issimus⟧.
⟦/⟧
Defective Comparison.
1. Positive lacking entirely,—
(Cf. ⟦b:prae⟧, ⟦i:in front of⟧.)  pr⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:former⟧,  pr⟦b:īmus⟧, ⟦i:first⟧
(Cf. ⟦b:citrā⟧, ⟦i:this side of⟧.)  citer⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:on this side⟧,  cit⟦b:imus⟧, ⟦i:near⟧.
(Cf. ⟦b:ultrā⟧, ⟦i:beyond⟧.)  ulter⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:farther⟧,  ult⟦b:imus⟧, ⟦i:farthest⟧.
(Cf. ⟦b:intrā⟧, ⟦i:within⟧.)  inter⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:inner⟧,  int⟦b:imus⟧, ⟦i:inmost⟧
(Cf. ⟦b:prope⟧, ⟦i:near⟧.)  prop⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:nearer⟧,  prox⟦b:imus⟧, ⟦i:nearest⟧.
(Cf. ⟦b:dē⟧, ⟦i:down⟧.)  dēter⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:inferior⟧,  dēter⟦b:rimus⟧, ⟦i:worst⟧.
(Cf. archaic ⟦b:potis⟧, ⟦i:possible⟧.)  pot⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:preferable⟧,  pot⟦b:issimus⟧, ⟦i:chiefest⟧
⟦/⟧
2. Positive occurring only in special cases,—
posterō diē, annō, ⟦i:etc. the following day⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧, posterī, ⟦i:descendants⟧,  poster⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:later⟧,  postr⟦b:ēmus⟧, ⟦i:latest⟧, ⟦i:last⟧. post⟦b:umus⟧, ⟦i:late-born⟧, ⟦i:posthumous⟧.
exteri, ⟦i:foreigners⟧, nātiōnēs exterae, ⟦i:foreign nations⟧,  exter⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:outer⟧  extr⟦b:ēmus⟧, ext⟦b:imus⟧, ⟦i:outermost⟧.
inferī, ⟦i:gods of the lower world⟧, Mare Inferum, ⟦i:Mediterranean Sea⟧,  īnfer⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:lower⟧,  īnf⟦b:imus⟧, ī⟦b:mus⟧, ⟦i:lowest⟧.
superī, ⟦i:gods above⟧, Mare Superum, ⟦i:Adriatic Sea⟧,  super⟦b:ior⟧, ⟦i:higher⟧,  supr⟦b:ēmus⟧, ⟦i:last⟧. sum⟦b:mus⟧, ⟦i:highest⟧.
⟦/⟧
3. Comparative lacking.
vetus, ⟦i:old⟧,  ——  veter⟦b:rimus⟧.
fīdus, ⟦i:faithful⟧,  ——  fīdis⟦b:simus⟧.
novus, ⟦i:new⟧,  ——  novis⟦b:simus⟧, ⟦i:last⟧.
sacer, ⟦i:sacred⟧,  ——  sacer⟦b:rimus⟧.
falsus, ⟦i:false⟧,  ——  fals⟦b:issimus⟧.
⟦/⟧
Also in some other words less frequently used.
4. Superlative lacking.
alacer, ⟦i:lively⟧,  alacr⟦b:ior⟧,  ——
ingēns, ⟦i:great⟧,  ingent⟦b:ior⟧,  ——
salūtāris, ⟦i:wholesome⟧,  salūtār⟦b:ior⟧,  ——
juvenis, ⟦i:young⟧,  jūn⟦b:ior⟧,  ——
senex, ⟦i:old⟧,  sen⟦b:ior⟧.  ——
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. The Superlative is lacking also in many adjectives in ⟦b:-ālis⟧, ⟦b:-īlis⟧, ⟦b:-ĭlis⟧, ⟦b:-bilis⟧, and in a few others.
Comparison by ⟦i:Magis⟧ and ⟦i:Maximē⟧.
Many adjectives do not admit terminational comparison, but form the Comparative and Superlative degrees by prefixing ⟦b:magis⟧ (⟦i:more⟧) and ⟦b:maximē⟧ (⟦i:most⟧). Here belong—
1. Many adjectives ending in ⟦b:-ālis⟧, ⟦b:-āris⟧, ⟦b:-idus⟧, ⟦b:-īlis⟧, ⟦b:-icus⟧, ⟦b:imus⟧, ⟦b:īnus⟧, ⟦b:-ōrus⟧.
2. Adjectives in ⟦b:-us⟧, preceded by a vowel; as, ⟦b:idōneus⟧, ⟦i:adapted⟧; ⟦b:arduus⟧, ⟦i:steep⟧; ⟦b:necessārius⟧, ⟦i:necessary⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Adjectives in ⟦b:-quus⟧, of course, do not come under this rule. The first ⟦b:u⟧ in such cases is not a vowel, but a consonant.
Adjectives not admitting Comparison.
Here belong—
1. Many adjectives, which, from the nature of their signification, do not admit of comparison; as, ⟦b:hodiernus⟧, ⟦i:of to-day⟧; ⟦b:annuus⟧, ⟦i:annual⟧; ⟦b:mortālis⟧, ⟦i:mortal⟧.
2. Some special words; as, ⟦b:mīrus⟧, ⟦b:gnārus⟧, ⟦b:merus⟧; and a few others.

title: Formation and Comparison of Adverbs
text:
Adverbs are for the most part derived from adjectives, and depend upon them for their comparison.
1. Adverbs derived from adjectives of the First and Second Declensions form the Positive by changing ⟦b:-ī⟧ of the Genitive Singular to ⟦b:-ē⟧; those derived from adjectives of the Third Declension, by changing ⟦b:-is⟧ of the Genitive Singular to ⟦b:-iter⟧; as,—
cārus,  cār⟦b:ē⟧, ⟦i:dearly⟧;
pulcher,  pulchr⟦b:ē⟧, ⟦i:beautifully⟧;
ācer,  ācr⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦i:fiercely⟧;
levis,  lev⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦i:lightly⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. But Adjectives in ⟦b:-ns⟧, and a few others, add ⟦b:-er⟧ (instead of ⟦b:-iter⟧), to form the Adverb; as,—
sapiēns,  sapient⟦b:er⟧, ⟦i:wisely⟧;
sollers,  sollert⟦b:er⟧, ⟦i:skillfully⟧.
⟦/⟧
Note ⟦b:audāx⟧, ⟦b:audācter⟧, ⟦i:boldly⟧.
2. The Comparative of all Adverbs regularly consists of the Accusative Singular Neuter of the Comparative of the Adjective; while the Superlative of the Adverb is formed by changing the ⟦b:-ī⟧ of the Genitive Singular of the Superlative of the Adjective to ⟦b:-ē⟧. Thus—
(cārus)  cār⟦b:ē⟧, ⟦i:dearly⟧,  cār⟦b:ius⟧,  cār⟦b:issimē⟧.
(pulcher)  pulchr⟦b:ē⟧, ⟦i:beautifully⟧,  pulchr⟦b:ius⟧,  pulcher⟦b:rimē⟧.
(ācer)  ācr⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦i:fiercely⟧,  ācr⟦b:ius⟧,  ācer⟦b:rimē⟧.
(levis)  lev⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦i:lightly⟧,  lev⟦b:ius⟧,  lev⟦b:issimē⟧.
(sapiēns)  sapien⟦b:ter⟧, ⟦i:wisely⟧,  sapient⟦b:ius⟧,  sapient⟦b:issimē⟧.
(audāx)  audāc⟦b:ter⟧, ⟦i:boldly⟧,  audāc⟦b:ius⟧,  audāc⟦b:issimē⟧.
⟦/⟧
Adverbs Peculiar in Comparison and Formation.
1.
benĕ, ⟦i:well⟧,  mel⟦b:ius⟧,  opt⟦b:imē⟧.
malĕ, ⟦i:ill⟧,  pe⟦b:jus⟧,  pess⟦b:imē⟧.
magnopere, ⟦i:greatly⟧,  mag⟦b:is⟧,  max⟦b:imē⟧.
multum, ⟦i:much⟧,  plūs,  plūr⟦b:imum⟧.
nōn multum, ⟦i:little⟧, parum,  min⟦b:us⟧,  min⟦b:imē⟧.
diū, ⟦i:long⟧,  diūt⟦b:ius⟧,  diūt⟦b:issimē⟧.
nēquiter, ⟦i:worthlessly⟧,  nēqu⟦b:ius⟧,  nēqu⟦b:issimē⟧.
saepe, ⟦i:often⟧,  saep⟦b:ius⟧,  saep⟦b:issimē⟧.
mātūrē, ⟦i:betimes⟧,  mātūr⟦b:ius⟧,  mātūr⟦b:rimē⟧. mātūr⟦b:issimē⟧.
prope, ⟦i:near⟧,  prop⟦b:ius⟧,  pro⟦b:ximē⟧.
nūper, ⟦i:recently⟧,  ——  nūper⟦b:rimē⟧.
——  pot⟦b:ius⟧, ⟦i:rather⟧,  pot⟦b:issimum⟧, ⟦i:especially⟧.
——  priu⟦b:s⟧, ⟦i:previously⟧, ⟦i:before⟧,  prī⟦b:mum⟧, ⟦i:first⟧.
secus, ⟦i:otherwise⟧,  sēt⟦b:ius⟧, ⟦i:less⟧.
⟦/⟧
2. A number of adjectives of the First and Second Declensions form an Adverb in ⟦b:-ō⟧, instead of ⟦b:-ē⟧; as,—
⟦b:crēbrō⟧, ⟦i:frequently⟧;  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:falsō⟧, ⟦i:falsely⟧;
⟦b:continuō⟧, ⟦i:immediately⟧;  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:subitō⟧, ⟦i:suddenly⟧;
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:rārō⟧, ⟦i:rarely⟧, and a few others.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. ⟦b:cito⟧, quickly, has ⟦b:-ŏ⟧.
3. A few adjectives employ the Accusative Singular Neuter as the Positive of the Adverb; as,—
⟦b:multum⟧, ⟦i:much⟧;  ⟦b:paulum⟧, ⟦i:little⟧;  ⟦b:facile⟧, ⟦i:easily⟧.
⟦/⟧
4. A few adjectives of the First and Second Declensions form the Positive in ⟦b:-iter⟧; as,—
⟦b:fīrmus⟧, ⟦b:fīrmiter⟧, ⟦i:firmly⟧;  ⟦b:hūmānus⟧, ⟦b:hūmāniter⟧, ⟦i:humanly⟧;
⟦b:largus⟧, ⟦b:largiter⟧, ⟦i:copiously⟧;  ⟦b:alius⟧, ⟦b:aliter⟧, ⟦i:otherwise⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. ⟦b:violentus⟧ has ⟦b:violenter⟧.
5. Various other adverbial suffixes occur, the most important of which are ⟦b:-tus⟧ and ⟦b:-tim⟧; as, ⟦b:antīquitus⟧, ⟦i:anciently⟧; ⟦b:paulātim⟧, ⟦i:gradually⟧.

title: Numerals
text:
Numerals may be divided into—
I. Numeral Adjectives, comprising—
⟦i:a⟧. ⟦i:Cardinals⟧; as, ⟦b:ūnus⟧, ⟦i:one⟧; ⟦b:duo⟧, ⟦i:two⟧; ⟦i:etc.⟧
⟦i:b⟧. ⟦i:Ordinals⟧; as, ⟦b:prīmus⟧, ⟦i:first⟧; ⟦b:secundus⟧, ⟦i:second⟧; ⟦i:etc.⟧
⟦i:c⟧. ⟦i:Distributives⟧; as, ⟦b:singulī⟧, ⟦i:one by one⟧; ⟦b:bīnī⟧, ⟦i:two by two⟧; ⟦i:etc.⟧
II. Numeral Adverbs; as, ⟦b:semel⟧, ⟦i:once⟧; ⟦b:bis⟧, ⟦i:twice⟧; ⟦i:etc.⟧
TABLE OF NUMERAL ADJECTIVES AND ADVERBS.
⟦.⟧  CARDINALS.  ORDINALS.  DISTRIBUTIVES.  ADVERBS.
1.  ūnus, ūna, ūnum  prīmus, ⟦i:first⟧  singulī, ⟦i:one by one⟧  semel, ⟦i:once⟧
2.  duo, duae, duo  secundus, ⟦i:second⟧  bīnī, ⟦i:two by two⟧  bis
3.  trēs, tria  tertius, ⟦i:third⟧  ternī (trīnī)  ter
4.  quattuor  quārtus, ⟦i:fourth⟧  quaternī  quater
5.  quīnque  quīntus, ⟦i:fifth⟧  quīnī  quīnquiēs
6.  sex  sextus  sēnī  sexiēs
7.  septem  septimus  septēnī  septiēs
8.  octō  octāvus  octōnī  octiēs
9.  novem  nōnus  novēnī  noviēs
10.  decem  decimus  dēnī  deciēs
11.  ūndecim  ūndecimus  ūndēnī  ūndeciēs
12.  duodecim  duodecimus  duodēnī  duodeciēs
13.  tredecim  tertius decimus  ternī denī  terdeciēs
14.  quattuordecim  quārtus decimus  quaternī denī  quaterdeciēs
15.  quīndecim  quīntus decimus  quīnī dēnī  quīnquiēs deciēs
16.  sēdecim, sexdecim  sextus decimus  sēnī dēnī  sexiēs deciēs
17.  septendecim  septimus decimus  septēnī dēnī  septiēs deciēs
18.  duodēvīgintī  duodēvīcēsimus  duodēvīcēnī  octiēs deciēs
19.  ūndēvīgintī  ūndēvīcēsimus  ūndēvīcēnī  noviēs deciēs
20.  vīgintī  vīcēsimus  vīcēnī  vīciēs
21.  vīgintī ūnus, ūnus et vīgintī  vīcēsimus prīmus, ūnus et vīcēsimus  vīcēnī singulī, singulī et vīcēni  vīciēs semel
22.  vīgintī duo, duo et vīgintī  vīcēsimus secundus, alter et vīcēsimus  vīcēnī bīnī, bīnī et vīcēnī  vīciēs bis
30.  trīgintā  trīcēsimus  trīcēnī  triciēs
40.  quadrāgintā  quadrāgēsimus  quadrāgēnī  quadrāgiēs
50.  quīnquāgintā  quīnquāgēsimus  quinquāgēnī  quīnquāgiēs
60.  sexāgintā  sexāgēsimus  sexāgēnī  sexāgiēs
70.  septuāgintā  septuāgēsimus  septuāgēnī  septuāgiēs
80.  octōgintā  octōgēsimus  octōgēnī  octōgiēs
90.  nōnāgintā  nōnāgēsimus  nōnāgēnī  nōnāgiēs
100.  centum  centēsimus  centēnī  centiēs
101.  centum ūnus, centum et ūnus  centēsimus prīmus, centēsimus et prīmus  centēnī singulī, centēnī et singulī  centiēs semel
200.  ducentī, -ae, -a  ducentēsimus  ducēnī  ducentiēs
300.  trecentī  trecentēsimus  trecēnī  trecentiēs
400.  quadringentī  quadringentēsimus  quadringēnī  quadringentiēs
500.  quīngentī  quīngentēsimus  quīngēnī  quīngentiēs
600.  sescentī  sescentēsimus  sescēnī  sescentiēs
700.  septingentī  septingentēsimus  septingēnī  septingentiēs
800.  octingentī  octingentēsimus  octingēnī  octingentiēs
900.  nōngentī  nōngentēsimus  nōngēnī  nōngentiēs
1,000.  mīlle  mīllēsimus  singula mīlia  mīliēs
2,000.  duo mīlia  bis mīllēsimus  bīna mīlia  bis mīliēs
100,000.  centum mīlia  centiēs mīllēsimus  centēna mīlia  centiēs mīliēs
1,000,000.  deciēs centēna mīlia  deciēs centiēs mīllēsimus  deciēs centēna mīlia  deciēs centiēs mīliēs
⟦/⟧
NOTE.— ⟦b:-ēnsimus⟧ and ⟦b:-iēns⟧ are often written in the numerals instead of ⟦b:-ēsimus⟧ and ⟦b:-iēs⟧.
Declension of the Cardinals.
1. The declension of ⟦b:ūnus⟧ has already been given under § 66.
2. ⟦b:Duo⟧ is declined as follows:—
⟦i:Nom.⟧  duo  duae  duo
⟦i:Gen.⟧  duōrum  duārum  duōrum
⟦i:Dat.⟧  duōbus  duābus  duōbus
⟦i:Acc.⟧  duōs, duo  duās  duo
⟦i:Abl.⟧  duōbus  duābus  duōbus
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. So ⟦b:ambō⟧, ⟦i:both⟧, except that its final ⟦b:o⟧ is long.
3. ⟦b:Trēs⟧ is declined,—
⟦i:Nom.⟧  trēs  tria
⟦i:Gen.⟧  trium  trium
⟦i:Dat.⟧  tribus  tribus
⟦i:Acc.⟧  trēs (trīs)  tria
⟦i:Abl.⟧  tribus  tribus
⟦/⟧
4. The hundreds (except ⟦b:centum⟧) are declined like the Plural of ⟦b:bonus⟧.
5. ⟦b:Mīlle⟧ is regularly an adjective in the Singular, and indeclinable. In the Plural it is a substantive (followed by the Genitive of the objects enumerated; § 201, 1), and is declined,—
⟦i:Nom.⟧  mīlia  ⟦i:Acc.⟧  mīlia
⟦i:Gen.⟧  mīlium  ⟦i:Voc.⟧  mīlia
⟦i:Dat.⟧  mīlibus  ⟦i:Abl.⟧  mīlibus
⟦/⟧
Thus ⟦b:mīlle hominēs⟧, ⟦i:a thousand men⟧; but ⟦b:duo mīlia hominum⟧, ⟦i:two thousand men⟧, literally ⟦i:two thousands of men⟧.
⟦i:a⟧. Occasionally the Singular admits the Genitive construction; as, ⟦b:mīlle hominum⟧.
6. Other Cardinals are indeclinable. Ordinals and Distributives are declined like Adjectives of the First and Second Declensions.
Peculiarities in the Use of Numerals.
1. The compounds from 21 to 99 may be expressed either with the larger or the smaller numeral first. In the latter case, ⟦b:et⟧ is used. Thus:—
⟦b:trīgintā sex⟧ or ⟦b:sex et trīgintā⟧, ⟦i:thirty-six⟧.
2. The numerals under 90, ending in 8 and 9, are often expressed by subtraction; as,—
⟦b:duodēvīgintī⟧, ⟦i:eighteen⟧ (but also ⟦b:octōdecim⟧);
⟦b:ūndēquadrāgintā⟧, ⟦i:thirty-nine⟧ (but also ⟦b:trīgintā novem⟧ or ⟦b:novem et trīgintā⟧).
3. Compounds over 100 regularly have the largest number first; the others follow without ⟦b:et⟧; as,—
⟦b:centum vīgintī septem⟧, ⟦i:one hundred and twenty-seven⟧.
⟦b:annō octingentēsimō octōgēsimō secundō⟧, ⟦i:in the year 882⟧.
Yet ⟦b:et⟧ may be inserted where the smaller number is either a digit or one of the tens; as,—
⟦b:centum et septem⟧, ⟦i:one hundred and seven⟧;
⟦b:centum et quadrāgintā⟧, ⟦i:one hundred and forty⟧.
4. The Distributives are used—
⟦i:a⟧) To denote ⟦i:so much each⟧, ⟦i:so many apiece⟧; as,—
⟦b:bīna talenta eīs dedit⟧, ⟦i:he gave them two talents each⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) When those nouns that are ordinarily Plural in form, but Singular in meaning, are employed in a Plural sense; as,—
⟦b:bīnae litterae⟧, ⟦i:two epistles⟧.
But in such cases, ⟦b:ūnī⟧ (not ⟦b:singulī⟧) is regularly employed for ⟦i:one⟧, and ⟦b:trīnī⟧ (not ⟦b:ternī⟧) for three; as,—
⟦b:ūnae litterae⟧, ⟦i:one epistle⟧; ⟦b:trīnae litterae⟧, ⟦i:three epistles⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) In multiplication; as,—
⟦b:bis bīna sunt quattuor⟧, ⟦i:twice two are four⟧.
⟦i:d⟧) Often in poetry, instead of the cardinals; as,—
⟦b:bīna hastīlia⟧, ⟦i:two spears⟧.

title: Personal Pronouns
text:
These correspond to the English ⟦i:I⟧, ⟦i:you⟧, ⟦i:he⟧, ⟦i:she⟧, ⟦i:it⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧, and are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  First Person.  Second Person.  Third Person.
⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  SINGULAR.
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ego, ⟦i:I⟧  tū, ⟦i:thou⟧  is, ⟦i:he⟧; ea, ⟦i:she⟧; id, ⟦i:it⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  meī  tuī  (For declension see § 87.)
⟦i:Dat.⟧  mihi  tibi[22]
⟦i:Acc.⟧  mē  tē
⟦i:Voc.⟧  ——  tū
⟦i:Abl.⟧  mē  tē
⟦.⟧  ⟦.⟧  PLURAL.

⟦i:Gen.⟧  nostrum, nostrī  vestrum, vestrī

1. A Dative Singular ⟦b:mī⟧ occurs in poetry.
2. Emphatic forms in ⟦b:-met⟧ are occasionally found; as, ⟦b:egomet⟧, ⟦i:I myself⟧; ⟦b:tibimet⟧, ⟦i:to you yourself⟧; ⟦b:tū⟧ has ⟦b:tūte⟧ and ⟦b:tūtemet⟧ (written also ⟦b:tūtimet⟧).
3. In early Latin, ⟦b:mēd⟧ and ⟦b:tēd⟧ occur as Accusative and Ablative forms.

title: Reflexive Pronouns
text:
These refer to the subject of the sentence or clause in which they stand; like ⟦i:myself⟧, ⟦i:yourself⟧, in '⟦i:I see myself⟧,' ⟦i:etc.⟧ They are declined as follows:—
⟦.⟧  ⟦i:First Person.⟧  ⟦i:Second Person.⟧  ⟦i:Third Person.⟧
⟦.⟧  Supplied by oblique cases of ⟦b:ego⟧.  Supplied by oblique cases of ⟦b:tū⟧.
⟦i:Gen.⟧  meī, ⟦i:of myself⟧  tuī, ⟦i:of thyself⟧  suī
⟦i:Dat.⟧  mihi, ⟦i:to myself⟧  tibi, ⟦i:to thyself⟧  sibi[22]
⟦i:Acc.⟧  mē, ⟦i:myself⟧  tē, ⟦i:thyself⟧  sē or sēsē
⟦i:Voc.⟧  ——  ——  ——
⟦i:Abl.⟧  mē, ⟦i:with myself⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧  tē, ⟦i:with thyself⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧  sē or sēsē
⟦/⟧
1. The Reflexive of the Third Person serves for ⟦i:all genders⟧ and for ⟦i:both numbers⟧. Thus ⟦b:sui⟧ may mean, ⟦i:of himself⟧, ⟦i:herself⟧, ⟦i:itself⟧, or ⟦i:of themselves⟧; and so with the other forms.
2. All of the Reflexive Pronouns have at times a ⟦i:reciprocal⟧ force; as,—
⟦b:inter sē pugnant⟧, ⟦i:they fight with each other⟧.
3. In early Latin, ⟦b:sēd⟧ occurs as Accusative and Ablative.

title: Possessive Pronouns
text:
These are strictly adjectives of the First and Second Declensions, and are inflected as such. They are—
⟦i:First Person.⟧ meus, -a, -um, ⟦i:my⟧; noster, nostra, nostrum, ⟦i:our⟧;  ⟦.⟧  ⟦i:Second Person.⟧ tuus, -a, -um, ⟦i:thy⟧; vester, vestra, vestrum, ⟦i:your⟧;
⟦.⟧  ⟦i:Third Person.⟧ suus, -a, -um, ⟦i:his⟧, ⟦i:her⟧, ⟦i:its⟧, ⟦i:their⟧.
⟦/⟧
1. ⟦b:Suus⟧ is exclusively Reflexive; as,—
⟦b:pater līberōs suōs amat⟧, ⟦i:the father loves his children⟧.
Otherwise, ⟦i:his⟧, ⟦i:her⟧, ⟦i:its⟧ are regularly expressed by the Genitive Singular of ⟦b:is⟧, ⟦i:viz.⟧ ⟦b:ejus⟧; and ⟦i:their⟧ by the Genitive Plural, ⟦b:eōrum⟧, ⟦b:eārum⟧.
2. The Vocative Singular Masculine of ⟦b:meus⟧ is ⟦b:mī⟧.
3. The enclitic ⟦b:-pte⟧ may be joined to the Ablative Singular of the Possessive Pronouns for the purpose of emphasis. This is particularly common in case of ⟦b:suō⟧, ⟦b:suā⟧; as, ⟦b:suōpte⟧, ⟦b:suāpte⟧.

title: Demonstrative Pronouns
text:
These point out an object as ⟦b:here⟧ or ⟦b:there⟧, or as ⟦b:previously mentioned⟧. They are—
⟦b:hīc⟧, ⟦i:this⟧ (where I am);
⟦b:iste⟧, ⟦i:that⟧ (where you are);
⟦b:ille⟧, ⟦i:that⟧ (something distinct from the speaker);
⟦b:is⟧, ⟦i:that⟧ (weaker than ⟦b:ille⟧);
⟦b:īdem⟧, ⟦i:the same⟧.
⟦b:Hīc⟧, ⟦b:iste⟧, and ⟦b:ille⟧ are accordingly the Demonstratives of the First, Second, and Third Persons respectively.

title: The Intensive Pronoun
text:
The Intensive Pronoun in Latin is ⟦b:ipse⟧. It corresponds to the English ⟦i:myself⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧, in '⟦i:I myself⟧, ⟦i:he himself.⟧'

text:

text:
The Interrogative Pronouns are ⟦b:quis⟧, ⟦i:who?⟧ (substantive) and ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦i:what? what kind of?⟧ (adjective).

⟦i:a⟧. An old Ablative ⟦b:quī⟧ occurs, in the sense of ⟦i:how? why?⟧
⟦i:b⟧. ⟦b:Quī⟧ is sometimes used for ⟦b:quis⟧ in Indirect Questions.
⟦i:c⟧. ⟦b:Quis⟧, when limiting words denoting persons, is sometimes an adjective. But in such cases ⟦b:quis homō⟧ = ⟦i:what man?⟧ whereas ⟦b:quī homō⟧ = ⟦i:what sort of man?⟧
⟦i:d⟧. ⟦b:Quis⟧ and ⟦b:quī⟧ may be strengthened by adding ⟦b:-nam⟧. Thus:—
Substantive:  ⟦b:quisnam⟧, ⟦i:who, pray?⟧ ⟦b:quidnam⟧, ⟦i:what, pray?⟧
Adjective:  ⟦b:quīnam⟧, ⟦b:quaenam⟧, ⟦b:quodnam⟧, ⟦i:of what kind, pray?⟧
⟦/⟧

text:
These have the general force of ⟦i:some one⟧, ⟦i:any one⟧.

1. In the Indefinite Pronouns, only the pronominal part is declined. Thus: Genitive Singular ⟦b:alicūjus⟧, ⟦b:cūjuslibet⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧
2. Note that ⟦b:aliquī⟧ has ⟦b:aliqua⟧ in the Nominative Singular Feminine, also in the Nominative and Accusative Plural Neuter. ⟦b:Quī⟧ has both ⟦b:qua⟧ and ⟦b:quae⟧ in these same cases.
3. ⟦b:Quīdam⟧ forms Accusative Singular ⟦b:quendam⟧, ⟦b:quandam⟧; Genitive Plural ⟦b:quōrundam⟧, ⟦b:quārundam⟧; the ⟦b:m⟧ being assimilated to ⟦b:n⟧ before ⟦b:d⟧.
4. ⟦b:Aliquis⟧ may be used adjectively, and (occasionally) ⟦b:aliquī⟧ substantively.
5. In combination with ⟦b:nē⟧, ⟦b:sī⟧, ⟦b:nisi⟧, ⟦b:num⟧, either ⟦b:quis⟧ or ⟦b:quī⟧ may stand as a Substantive. Thus: ⟦b:sī quis⟧ or ⟦b:sī quī⟧.
6. ⟦b:Ecquis⟧, ⟦i:any one⟧, though strictly an Indefinite, generally has interrogative force. It has both substantive and adjective forms,—substantive, ⟦b:ecquis⟧, ⟦b:ecquid⟧; adjective, ⟦b:ecquī⟧, ⟦b:ecquae⟧ and ⟦b:ecqua⟧, ⟦b:ecquod⟧.
7. ⟦b:Quisquam⟧ is not used in the Plural.
8. There are two Indefinite Relatives,—⟦b:quīcumque⟧ and ⟦b:quisquis⟧, ⟦i:whoever⟧. ⟦b:Quīcumque⟧ declines only the first part; ⟦b:quisquis⟧ declines both but has only ⟦b:quisquis⟧, ⟦b:quidquid⟧, ⟦b:quōquō⟧, in common use.

title: Pronominal Adjectives
text:
The following adjectives, also, frequently have pronominal force:—
1.
⟦b:alius⟧, ⟦i:another;⟧  ⟦b:alter⟧, ⟦i:the other;⟧
⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦i:which of two?⟧ (interr.); ⟦i:whichever of two⟧ (rel.);  ⟦b:neuter⟧, ⟦i:neither;⟧
⟦b:ūnus⟧, ⟦i:one⟧;  ⟦b:nūllus⟧, ⟦i:no one⟧ (in oblique cases)
⟦/⟧
2. The compounds,—
⟦b:uterque⟧, ⟦b:utraque⟧, ⟦b:utrumque⟧, ⟦i:each of two;⟧
⟦b:utercumque⟧, ⟦b:utracumque⟧, ⟦b:utrumcumque⟧, ⟦i:whoever of two;⟧
⟦b:uterlibet⟧, ⟦b:utralibet⟧, ⟦b:utrumlibet⟧, ⟦i:either one you please;⟧
⟦b:utervīs⟧, ⟦b:utravīs⟧, ⟦b:utrumvīs⟧, ⟦i:either one you please;⟧
⟦b:alteruter⟧, ⟦b:alterutra⟧, ⟦b:alterutrum⟧, ⟦i:the one or the other⟧.
In these, ⟦b:uter⟧ alone is declined. The rest of the word remains unchanged, except in case of ⟦b:alteruter⟧, which may decline both parts; as,—
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:alteruter⟧  ⟦b:altera utra⟧  ⟦b:alterum utrum⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:alterius utrīus⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧
⟦/⟧
A Verb is a word which asserts something; as, ⟦b:est⟧, ⟦i:he is⟧; ⟦b:amat⟧, ⟦i:he loves⟧. The Inflection of Verbs is called Conjugation.
Verbs have Voice, Mood, Tense, Number, and Person:—
1. Two Voices,—Active and Passive.
2. Three Moods,—Indicative, Subjunctive, Imperative.
3. Six Tenses,—
Present,  Perfect,
Imperfect,  Pluperfect,
Future,  Future Perfect.
⟦/⟧
But the Subjunctive lacks the Future and Future Perfect; while the Imperative employs only the Present and Future.
4. Two Numbers,—Singular and Plural.
5. Three Persons,—First, Second, and Third.
These make up the so-called ⟦i:Finite Verb⟧. Besides this, we have the following Noun and Adjective Forms:—
1. Noun Forms,—Infinitive, Gerund, and Supine.
2. Adjective Forms,—Participles (including the Gerundive).
The Personal Endings of the Verb are,—
⟦.⟧  Active.  Passive.
⟦i:Sing⟧. 1.  ⟦b:-ō; -m; -ī⟧ (Perf. Ind.);  ⟦b:-r⟧.
2.  ⟦b:-s⟧; ⟦b:-stī⟧ (Perf Ind.); ⟦b:-tō⟧ or wanting (Impv.);  ⟦b:-rīs⟧, ⟦b:-re⟧; ⟦b:-re⟧, ⟦b:-tor⟧ (Impv.).
3.  ⟦b:-t; -tō⟧ (Impv.);  ⟦b:-tur; -tor⟧ (Impv.).
⟦i:Plu⟧. 1.  ⟦b:-mus;⟧  ⟦b:-mur⟧.
2.  ⟦b:-tis⟧; ⟦b:-stis⟧ (Perf. Ind.); ⟦b:-te⟧, ⟦b:-tōte⟧ (Impv.);  ⟦b:-minī⟧.
3.  ⟦b:-nt; -ērunt⟧ (Perf Ind.); ⟦b:-ntō⟧ (Impv.);  ⟦b:-ntur; -ntor⟧ (Impv.).
⟦/⟧

title: Verb Stems
text:
Conjugation consists in appending certain endings to the Stem. We distinguish three different stems in a fully inflected verb,—
⟦b:I. Present Stem⟧, from which are formed—
1. Present, Imperfect, and Future Indicative,
2. Present and Imperfect Subjunctive,
3. The Imperative,
4. The Present Infinitive,
- (Active and Passive.)
5. The Present Active Participle, the Gerund, and Gerundive.
⟦b:II. Perfect Stem⟧, from which are formed—
1. Perfect, Pluperfect, and Future Perfect Indicative,
2. Perfect and Pluperfect Subjunctive,
3. Perfect Infinitive,
- (Active.)
⟦b:III. Participial Stem⟧, from which are formed—
1. Perfect Participle,
2. Perfect, Pluperfect, and Future Perfect Indicative,
3. Perfect and Pluperfect Subjunctive,
4. Perfect Infinitive,
- (Passive.)
Apparently from the same stem, though really of different origin, are the Supine, the Future Active Participle, the Future Infinitive Active and Passive.

title: The Four Conjugations
text:
There are in Latin four regular Conjugations, distinguished from each other by the vowel of the termination of the Present Infinitive Active, as follows:—
CONJUGATION.  INFINITIVE TERMINATION.  DISTINGUISHING VOWEL.
I.  ⟦b:-āre⟧  ⟦b:ā⟧
II.  ⟦b:-ēre⟧  ⟦b:ē⟧
III.  ⟦b:-ĕre⟧  ⟦b:ĕ⟧
IV.  ⟦b:-īre⟧  ⟦b:ī⟧
⟦/⟧
PRINCIPAL PARTS. The Present Indicative, Present Infinitive, Perfect Indicative, and the Perfect Participle constitute the ⟦b:Principal Parts⟧ of a Latin verb,—so called because they contain the different stems, from which the full conjugation of the verb may be derived.

title: Verbs in -Iō of the Third Conjugation
text:
1. Verbs in ⟦b:-iō⟧ of the Third Conjugation take the endings of the Fourth Conjugation wherever the latter endings have two successive vowels. This occurs only in the Present System.
2. Here belong—
⟦i:a⟧) ⟦b:capiō⟧, ⟦i:to take⟧; ⟦b:cupiō⟧, ⟦i:to desire⟧; ⟦b:faciō⟧, ⟦i:to make⟧; ⟦b:fodiō⟧, ⟦i:to dig⟧; ⟦b:fugiō⟧, ⟦i:to flee⟧; ⟦b:jaciō⟧, ⟦i:to throw⟧; ⟦b:pariō⟧, ⟦i:to bear⟧; ⟦b:quatiō⟧, ⟦i:to shake⟧; ⟦b:rapiō⟧, ⟦i:to seize⟧; ⟦b:sapiō⟧, ⟦i:to taste⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) Compounds of ⟦b:laciō⟧ and ⟦b:speciō⟧ (both ante-classical); as, ⟦b:alliciō⟧, ⟦i:entice⟧; ⟦b:cōnspiciō⟧, ⟦i:behold⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) The deponents ⟦b:gradior⟧, ⟦i:to go⟧; ⟦b:morior⟧, ⟦i:to die⟧, ⟦b:patior⟧, ⟦i:to suffer⟧.

title: Deponent Verbs
text:
Deponent Verbs have in the main Passive ⟦i:forms⟧ with Active or Neuter ⟦i:meaning⟧. But—
⟦i:a⟧. They have the following Active forms: Future Infinitive, Present and Future Participles, Gerund, and Supine.
⟦i:b⟧. They have the following Passive meanings: always in the Gerundive, and sometimes in the Perfect Passive Participle; as—
⟦b:sequendus⟧, ⟦i:to be followed⟧; ⟦b:adeptus⟧, ⟦i:attained⟧.
Paradigms of Deponent Verbs are—
I. Conj.  ⟦b:mīror⟧, ⟦b:mīrārī⟧, ⟦b:mīrātus sum⟧, ⟦i:admire⟧.
II. Conj.  ⟦b:vereor⟧, ⟦b:vererī⟧, ⟦b:veritus sum⟧, ⟦i:fear⟧.
III. Conj.  ⟦b:sequor⟧, ⟦b:sequī⟧, ⟦b:secūtus sum⟧, ⟦i:follow⟧.
IV. Conj.  ⟦b:largior⟧, ⟦b:largīrī⟧, ⟦b:largītus sum⟧, ⟦i:give⟧.
III. (in ⟦b:-ior⟧)  ⟦b:patior⟧, ⟦b:patī⟧, ⟦b:passus sum⟧, ⟦i:suffer⟧.
⟦/⟧

title: Semi-deponents
text:
1. Semi-Deponents are verbs which have the Present System in the Active Voice, but the Perfect System in the Passive without change of meaning. Here belong—
⟦b:audeō⟧,  ⟦b:audēre⟧,  ⟦b:ausus sum⟧, ⟦i:to dare⟧.
⟦b:gaudeō⟧,  ⟦b:gaudēre⟧,  ⟦b:gāvīsus sum⟧, ⟦i:to rejoice⟧.
⟦b:soleō⟧,  ⟦b:solēre⟧,  ⟦b:solitus sum⟧, ⟦i:to be wont⟧.
⟦b:fīdō⟧,  ⟦b:fīdere⟧,  ⟦b:fīsus sum⟧, ⟦i:to trust⟧.
⟦/⟧
2. The following verbs have a Perfect Passive Participle with Active meaning:—
⟦b:adolēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow up⟧;  ⟦b:adultus⟧, ⟦i:having grown up⟧,
⟦b:cēnāre⟧, ⟦i:dine⟧;  ⟦b:cēnātus⟧, ⟦i:having dined⟧.
⟦b:placēre⟧, ⟦i:please⟧;  ⟦b:placitus⟧, ⟦i:having pleased⟧, ⟦i:agreeable⟧.
⟦b:prandēre⟧, ⟦i:lunch⟧;  ⟦b:prānsus⟧, ⟦i:having lunched⟧.
⟦b:pōtāre⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧;  ⟦b:pōtus⟧, ⟦i:having drunk⟧.
⟦b:jūrāre⟧, ⟦i:swear⟧;  ⟦b:jūrātus⟧, ⟦i:having sworn⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. ⟦b:Jūrātus⟧ is used in a passive sense also.
3. ⟦b:Revertor⟧ and ⟦b:dēvertor⟧ both regularly form their Perfect in the Active Voice; ⟦i:viz⟧.—
⟦b:revertor⟧,  ⟦b:revertī⟧ (Inf.),  ⟦b:revertī⟧ (Perf.), ⟦i:to return⟧.
⟦b:dēvertor⟧,  ⟦b:dēvertī⟧ (Inf.),  ⟦b:dēvertī⟧ (Perf.), ⟦i:to turn aside⟧.
⟦/⟧

title: Periphrastic Conjugation
text:
There are two Periphrastic Conjugations,—the Active and the Passive. The Active is formed by combining the Future Active Participle with the auxiliary ⟦b:sum⟧, the Passive by combining the Gerundive with the same auxiliary.
⟦=⟧⟦b:Active Periphrastic Conjugation.⟧  ⟦b:INDICATIVE MOOD.⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus⟧ (⟦b:-a⟧, ⟦b:-um⟧) ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:I am about to love⟧.
⟦i:Inf.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus eram⟧, ⟦i:I was about to love⟧.
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus erō⟧, ⟦i:I shall be about to love⟧.
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus fuī⟧, ⟦i:I have been (was) about to love⟧.
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus fueram⟧, ⟦i:I had been about to love⟧.
⟦i:Fut. P.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus fuerō⟧, ⟦i:I shall have been about to love⟧.
⟦=⟧⟦b:SUBJUNCTIVE.⟧

⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus essem⟧, ⟦i:I should be about to love⟧.
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus fuerim⟧, ⟦i:I may have been about to love⟧.
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus fuissem⟧, ⟦i:I should have been about to love⟧.
⟦=⟧⟦b:INFINITIVE.⟧

⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:amātūrus fuisse⟧, ⟦i:to have been about to love⟧.

⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:amandus erō⟧, ⟦i:I shall deserve to be loved⟧.
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:amandus fuī⟧, ⟦i:I was to be loved⟧.

title: Peculiarities of Conjugation
text:
1. Perfects in ⟦b:-āvī⟧, ⟦b:-ēvī⟧, and ⟦b:-īvī⟧, with the forms derived from them, often drop the ⟦b:ve⟧ or ⟦b:vi⟧ before endings beginning with ⟦b:r⟧ or ⟦b:s⟧. So also ⟦b:nōvī⟧ (from ⟦b:nōscō⟧) and the compounds of ⟦b:mōvī⟧ (from ⟦b:moveō⟧). Thus:—
amāvistī  amāstī  dēlēvistī  dēlēstī
amāvisse  amāsse  dēlēvisse  dēlēsse
amāvērunt  amārunt  dēlēvērunt  dēlērunt
amāverim  amārim  dēlēverim  dēlērim
amāveram  amāram  dēlēveram  dēlēram
amāverō  amārō  dēlēverō  dēlērō
nōvistī  nōstī  nōverim  nōrim
nōvisse  nōsse  nōveram  nōram
audīvistī  audīstī  audīvisse  audīsse
⟦/⟧
2. In the Gerund and Gerundive of the Third and Fourth Conjugations, the endings ⟦b:-undus⟧, ⟦b:-undī⟧, often occur instead of ⟦b:-endus⟧ and ⟦b:-endī⟧, as ⟦b:faciundus⟧, ⟦b:faciundī⟧.
3. ⟦b:Dīcō⟧, ⟦b:dūcō⟧, ⟦b:faciō⟧, form the Imperatives, ⟦b:dīc⟧, ⟦b:dūc⟧, ⟦b:fac⟧. But compounds of ⟦b:faciō⟧ form the Imperative in ⟦b:-fice⟧, as ⟦b:cōnfice⟧. Compounds of ⟦b:dīcō⟧, ⟦b:dūcō⟧, accent the ultima; as, ⟦b:ēdū´c⟧, ⟦b:ēdī´c⟧.
4. Archaic and Poetic forms:—
⟦i:a⟧. The ending ⟦b:-ier⟧ in the Present Infinitive Passive; as, ⟦b:amārier⟧, ⟦b:monērier⟧, ⟦b:dīcier⟧, for ⟦b:amārī⟧, ⟦b:monērī⟧, ⟦b:dīcī⟧.
⟦i:b⟧. The ending ⟦b:-ībam⟧ for ⟦b:-iēbam⟧ in Imperfects of the Fourth Conjugation, and ⟦b:-ībō⟧ for ⟦b:-iam⟧ in Futures; as, ⟦b:scībam⟧, ⟦b:scībō⟧, for ⟦b:sciēbam⟧, ⟦b:sciam⟧.
⟦i:c⟧. Instead of the fuller forms, in such words as ⟦b:dīxistī⟧, ⟦b:scrīpsistis⟧, ⟦b:surrēxisse⟧, we sometimes find ⟦b:dīxtī⟧, ⟦b:scrīpstis⟧, ⟦b:surrēxe⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧
⟦i:d⟧. The endings ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦b:-īs⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧ (for ⟦b:-am⟧, ⟦b:-ās⟧, ⟦i:etc.⟧) occur in a few Subjunctive forms; as, ⟦b:edim⟧ (⟦i:eat⟧), ⟦b:duint⟧, ⟦b:perduint⟧.
5. In the Future Active and Perfect Passive Infinitive, the auxiliary ⟦b:esse⟧ is often omitted; as, ⟦b:āctūrum⟧ for ⟦b:ācturum esse⟧; ⟦b:ējectus⟧ for ⟦b:ējectus esse⟧.
Formation of the Present Stem.

title: Formation of the Verb Stems
text:
Many verbs employ the simple Verb Stem for the Present Stem; as, ⟦b:dīcere⟧, ⟦b:amāre⟧, ⟦b:monēre⟧, ⟦b:audīre⟧. Others modify the Verb Stem to form the Present, as follows:—
1. By appending the vowels, ⟦b:ā⟧, ⟦b:ē⟧, ⟦b:ī⟧; as,—
⟦.⟧  Present Stem  Verb Stem
⟦b:juvāre⟧,  ⟦b:juvā-⟧  ⟦b:juv-⟧.
⟦b:augēre⟧,  ⟦b:augē-⟧  ⟦b:aug-⟧.
⟦b:vincīre⟧,  ⟦b:vincī-⟧  ⟦b:vinc-⟧.
⟦/⟧
2. By adding ⟦b:i⟧, as ⟦b:capiō⟧, Present Stem ⟦b:capi-⟧ (Verb Stem ⟦b:cap-⟧).
3. By the insertion of ⟦b:n⟧ (⟦b:m⟧ before labial-mutes) before the final consonant of the Verb Stem; as, ⟦b:fundō⟧ (Stem ⟦b:fud-⟧), ⟦b:rumpō⟧ (Stem ⟦b:rup-⟧).
4. By appending ⟦b:-n⟧ to the Verb Stem; as,—
⟦b:cern-ō⟧  ⟦b:pell-ō⟧ (for ⟦b:pel-nō⟧).
⟦/⟧
5. By appending ⟦b:t⟧ to the Verb Stem; as,—
⟦b:flect-ō.⟧
⟦/⟧
6. By appending ⟦b:sc⟧ to the Verb Stem; as,—
⟦b:crēsc-ō⟧.  ⟦b:scīsc-ō⟧.
⟦/⟧
7. By Reduplication, that is, by prefixing the initial consonant of the Verb Stem with ⟦b:i⟧; as,—
⟦b:gi-gn-ō⟧ (root ⟦b:gen-⟧),  ⟦b:si-st-ō⟧ (root ⟦b:sta-⟧).
⟦/⟧
Formation of the Perfect Stem.
The Perfect Stem is formed from the Verb Stem—
1. By adding ⟦b:v⟧ (in case of Vowel Stems); as,—
⟦b:amāv-ī⟧,  ⟦b:dēlēv-ī⟧,  ⟦b:audīv-ī⟧.
⟦/⟧
2. By adding ⟦b:u⟧ (in case of some Consonant Stems); as,—
⟦b:strepu-ī⟧,  ⟦b:genu-ī⟧,  ⟦b:alu-ī⟧.
⟦/⟧
3. By adding ⟦b:s⟧ (in case of most Consonant Stems); as,—
⟦b:carp-ō⟧,  Perfect  ⟦b:carps-ī⟧.
⟦b:scrīb-ō⟧,  "  ⟦b:scrīps-ī⟧ (for ⟦b:scrīb-sī⟧).
⟦b:rīd-eō⟧,  "  ⟦b:rīs-ī⟧ (for ⟦b:rīd-sī⟧).
⟦b:sent-iō⟧,  "  ⟦b:sēns-ī⟧ (for ⟦b:sent-sī⟧).
⟦b:dīc-ō⟧,  "  ⟦b:dīx-ī⟧ (⟦i:i.e.⟧ ⟦b:dīc-sī⟧).
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. Note that before the ending ⟦b:-sī⟧ a Dental Mute (⟦b:t⟧, ⟦b:d⟧) is lost; a Guttural Mute (⟦b:c⟧, ⟦b:g⟧) unites with ⟦b:s⟧ to form ⟦b:x⟧; while the Labial ⟦b:b⟧ is changed to ⟦b:p⟧.
4. Without addition. Of this formation there are three types:—
⟦i:a⟧) The Verb Stem is reduplicated by prefixing the initial consonant with the following vowel or ⟦b:e⟧; as,—
⟦b:currō⟧,  Perfect  ⟦b:cu-currī⟧.
⟦b:poscō⟧,  "  ⟦b:po-poscī⟧.
⟦b:pellō⟧,  "  ⟦b:pe-pulī⟧.
⟦/⟧
NOTE 1.—Compounds, with the exception of ⟦b:dō⟧, ⟦b:stō⟧, ⟦b:sistō⟧, ⟦b:discō⟧, ⟦b:poscō⟧, omit the reduplication. Thus: ⟦b:com-pulī⟧, but ⟦b:re-poposcī⟧.
NOTE 2.—Verbs beginning with ⟦b:sp⟧ or ⟦b:st⟧ retain both consonants in the reduplication, but drop ⟦b:s⟧ from the stem; as, ⟦b:spondeō⟧, ⟦b:spo-pondī⟧; ⟦b:stō⟧, ⟦b:stetī⟧.
⟦i:b⟧) The short vowel of the Verb Stem is lengthened; as, ⟦b:legō⟧, ⟦b:lēgī⟧; ⟦b:agō⟧, ⟦b:ēgī⟧. Note that ⟦b:ă⟧ by this process becomes ⟦b:ē⟧.
⟦i:c⟧) The vowel of the Verb Stem is unchanged; as, ⟦b:vertō⟧, ⟦b:vertī⟧; ⟦b:minuō⟧, ⟦b:minuī⟧.
Formation of the Participial Stem.
The Perfect Passive Participle, from which the Participial Stem is derived by dropping ⟦b:-us⟧, is formed:—
1. By adding ⟦b:-tus⟧ (sometimes to the Present Stem, sometimes to the Verb Stem); as,—
⟦b:amā-re⟧,  Participle  ⟦b:amā-tus⟧.
⟦b:dēlē-re⟧,  "  ⟦b:dēlē-tus⟧,
⟦b:audī-re⟧,  "  ⟦b:audī-tus⟧,
⟦b:leg-ere⟧,  "  ⟦b:lēc-tus⟧,
⟦b:scrīb-ere⟧,  "  ⟦b:scrīp-tus⟧,
⟦b:sentī-re⟧,  "  ⟦b:sēn-sus⟧ (for ⟦b:sent-tus⟧).
⟦b:caed-ere⟧,  "  ⟦b:cae-sus⟧ (for ⟦b:caed-tus⟧).
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. Note that ⟦b:g⟧, before ⟦b:t⟧, becomes ⟦b:c⟧ (see § 8, 5); ⟦b:b⟧ becomes ⟦b:p⟧; while ⟦b:dt⟧ or ⟦b:tt⟧ becomes ⟦b:ss⟧, which is then often simplified to ⟦b:s⟧ (§ 8, 2).
2. After the analogy of Participles like ⟦b:sēnsus⟧ and ⟦b:caesus⟧, where ⟦b:-sus⟧ arises by phonetic change, ⟦b:-sus⟧ for ⟦b:-tus⟧ is added to other Verb Stems; as,—
⟦b:lāb-ī⟧,  Participle  ⟦b:lāp-sus⟧.
⟦b:fīg-ere⟧,  "  ⟦b:fī-xus⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦i:a⟧. The same consonant changes occur in appending this ending ⟦b:-sus⟧ to the stem as in the case of the Perfect ending ⟦b:-si⟧ (see § 118, 3, ⟦i:a⟧).
3. A few Verbs form the Participle in ⟦b:-ĭtus⟧; as,—
⟦b:domā-re⟧,  ⟦b:dom-ĭtus⟧.
⟦b:monē-re⟧,  ⟦b:mon-ĭtus⟧.
⟦/⟧
4. The Future Active Participle is usually identical in its stem with the Perfect Passive Participle; as, ⟦b:amā-tus⟧, ⟦b:amātūrus⟧; ⟦b:moni-tus⟧, ⟦b:monitūrus⟧. But—
⟦b:juvā-re⟧,  Perf. Partic.  ⟦b:jūtus⟧,  has Fut. Act. Partic.  ⟦b:juvātūrus⟧.
⟦b:lavā-re⟧,  "  ⟦b:lautus⟧,  "  ⟦b:lavātūrus⟧.

First (⟦i:Ā⟧-) Conjugation.

title: List of the Most Important Verbs, with Principal Parts
text:
I. PERFECT IN ⟦b:-VĪ⟧.
amō  amāre  amāvī  amātus  ⟦i:love⟧
⟦/⟧
All regular verbs of the First Conjugation follow this model.

V. DEPONENTS.
These are all regular, and follow ⟦i:mīror⟧, ⟦i:mīrārī⟧, ⟦i:mīrātus sum⟧.

cōnsulō  cōnsulere  cōnsuluī  cōnsultus  ⟦i:consult⟧

ponō  pōnere  posuī  positus  ⟦i:place⟧
ob-linō  oblinere  oblēvī  oblitus  ⟦i:smear⟧

cōnserō  cōnserere  cōnsēvī  cōnsitus  ⟦i:plant⟧

dēcernō  dēcernere  dēcrēvī  dēcrētus  ⟦i:decide⟧
spernō  spernere  sprēvī  sprētus  ⟦i:scorn⟧
sternō  sternere  strāvī  strātus  ⟦i:spread⟧
prō-sternō  prōsternere  prōstrāvī  prōstrātus  ⟦i:overthrow⟧

and a few others.

II. VERBS WITH PRESENT STEM ENDING IN ⟦b:-U⟧.

imbuō  imbuere  imbuī  imbūtus  ⟦i:moisten⟧

obruō  obruere  obruī  obrutus  ⟦i:overwhelm⟧
acuō  acuere  acuī  ——  ⟦i:sharpen⟧
arguō  arguere  arguī  ——  ⟦i:accuse⟧
congruō  congruere  congruī  ——  ⟦i:agree⟧
